title: Board of Aldermen Meeting - April 1, 2019
text: Town of Harmony Meeting Minutes Town of Harmony North Carolina 3389 Harmony Highway, Harmony, NC 28634 704-546-2339 DATE: April 1, 2019 TIME: 7:00 PM ATTENDEES: Lee Matney, Mayor John Ray Campbell – Alderman Julia Clanton – Alderman Doug Galliher – Alderman Scotty Harris - Alderman AGENDA: Call to Order: Mayor Matney Invocation: Alderman Campbell Pledge of Allegiance: Alderman Clanton Approval of previous Months Minutes Julia Clanton made a motion to approve the minutes of the March 4th, 2019 meeting – Scotty Harris seconded the motion. Motion carried. Public Comment Period: Notes on the Comment Period Each speaker is asked to limit comments to 3 minutes. The total comment period will be 15 minutes or less. Citizens should sign up with the Town Clerk to speak to the board by 3:00pm on the Thursday prior to the meeting on Monday night. At the time of sign-up, speakers should state their subject or the matter of concern. Speakers should be aware the Town Board is interested in hearing the concerns of the speakers; however speakers should not expect Board action or deliberation on the subject matter brought up during the Public Comment segment. Topics requiring further investigation will be referred to the appropriate town officials or staff and may be scheduled for a future agenda. Thank you for your consideration of the Town Council, staff, and other speakers. . Old Business: No old business New Business Discussion was held about complaints of aggressive dogs in the park, and dog owners not cleaning up after their dogs. Mayor Matney will work on an ordinance amendment addressing these problems and present them to the Council at the May meeting. Problems with cows and now goats inside the town limits at the residence of Jose Rodriquez on Harmony Hwy north was again brought up. Mr. Rodriquez was sent a letter outlining the ordinance regarding cows, etc. inside the town limits. Mayor will meet with Sheriff Campbell prior to the May meeting to discuss enforcing the town ordinances. Complaints about 4 wheelers on Tomlinson Avenue and on Town property was also discussed. “No Trespassing” signs will be put up on wooded area town owns and also on the 10 acre property owned by the town. Mayor will inform Gene Powers of this action. Letter of Engagement, pertaining to the June 30, 2019 audit to be performed by Eddie Carrick, CPA was explained the council. Scotty Harris signed the letter along with Mayor Matney. Scotty Harris requested that maintenance go to the entrance at the Waste Water Treatment Plant on Windmill Court and clean the ditch line. Julia Clanton asked the council about the possibility of having a sidewalk and speed bumps installed on John Deere Drive. Mayor Matney will talk to someone to see if this is a county or town road. Personnel – Mayor Matney told the Council that we need to hire someone to be trained to work in office in the event that the town clerk has to be out of the office for an extended period of time. Further discussion will be held at a later date. Adjournment John Ray Campbell made a motion to adjourn. Julia Clanton seconded. Motion carried. Town Clerk___________________________________Mayor____________________________

title: Board of Aldermen Meeting - April 3, 2023
text: Town of Harmony 3389 Harmony Hwy, Harmony, NC 28634 704-546-2339 DATE: April 3, 2023 TIME: 4:00 PM ATTENDEES: Lee Matney, Mayor N Sankey Gaither - Council Member Julia Clanton - Council Member Doug Galliher – Council Member Scotty Harris – Council Member Wanda Edwards – Town Clerk AGENDA: Call to Order: Mayor Matney Invocation: Council Member Harris Pledge of Allegiance: Council Member Clanton Approval of minutes: Scotty Harris made a motion to approve the March 6th minutes. Julia Clanton seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. Julia made a motion to approve the Closed Session minutes. Buddy Gaither seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. Doug Galliher made a motion to approve the minutes of the Sewer Minutes. Scotty seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. Public Comment Period: Each speaker is asked to limit comments to 3 minutes. The total comment period will be 15 minutes or less. Citizens should sign up with the Town Clerk to speak to the board by 3:00 pm on the Thursday prior to the meeting on Monday night. At the time of sign-up speakers should state their subject or the matter of concern Speakers should be the Town Board is interested in hearing the concerns of the speakers, however speakers should not expect Board action or deliberation on the subject matter brought up during the Public Comment segment. Topics requiring further investigation will be referred to the appropriate town officials or staff and may be scheduled for a future agenda. Thank you for your consideration of the Town Council, staff and other speakers. Shawn Turner spoke to the Council – he would like to see a committee formed for whatever is coming forth from the State pertaining to the 20/45 plan for growth going forward. He also spoke about a problem he has with the Family Dollar. He has property that adjoins the Family Dollar property. He said their dumpster overflows onto his property. He has spoken to them about it but nothing has been done. He asked Mayor Matney if he would speak to a District Manager about the problem. Shawn also asked about leasing the field next to his house that is being leased by Gene Powers. He offered to pay more than Gene pays. He said his well is within 16’ of the field and that if Gene is spraying chemicals, he will be back with his attorney. He was told that Gene has to notify the Town in writing within 30 days of the end of the lease if he chooses not to renew the lease. OLD BUSINESS: Alex Grant spoke to the Council about the columbarium – he said the one at Winthrop Church had 48 niches. The columbarium can face east or west. The niche is 12x12x12. You can put 2 urns in each niche. No flowers are allowed at the columbarium. Door - recommended that it be engraved on granite on door itself instead of using bronze plaques. Door can hold name/date – 3 lines. Extra cost for wording or door. Cost for niche is the same if you put 2 urns in the niche. Board Term – Ms. Dixon , Town Attorney, spoke to the board. She said the way the Board is set up now could put the board in a precarious situation if a completely new board would happen to be voted in at some point. We are beginning the process of amending the Town Ordinance to stagger the term limits of the town council so someone with experience will always be on the board. Ms. Dixon said we will need to amend the ordinances to modify the Town Charter. We need to propose in session what we want to amend ( terms & add council member) Reduce it to writing Publish it as usual – no closer than 10 days – publish it again Call public meeting Adopt When it is adopted, Town Clerk must file a certified true copy of any amendment adopted with the NC Secretary of State and the NC Legislative Library. Ms. Dixon said that most towns have an uneven number of council members at large. We have to decide who is going to run. Jeff Jones – Harmony Waste Water ORC spoke to the group about the applications he had received for RFQ - the “On Call Engineering Services”. He also answered some questions that had been brought up in the sewer meeting (1) what is our sewer capacity – permit says 80,000 gal. per day – option 100,00 per day . 21,000 – 25,000 gal is what we run now. When we get to 80,000 gallons, we need to start planning. At 90,000 gal. state requires us to do something. We had 4 engineering firms respond to our RFQ so we can move forward with AIA. Those responding were: McGill, Wooten, TRC, and Withers Ravenal. Jeff wants to set a meeting in 2 weeks to pick a firm or he can make a recommendation now. Wooten is one of his top choices. TRC seems to be going through a lot of changes and are not too stable. We paid Withers $5,000 to get us funded. Jeff’s recommendation is McGill. They are the only ones that called and set up a meeting with him. They came highly recommended from Sparta and they are from Hickory. We will meet on April 17th at 4 p.m. NEW BUSINESS: Discussion was brought up about safety measures that Deputy Marty Liles suggested should be made to the Town Hall. He suggested that we replace the hall door with a heavy door that has a key pad entry. He also would like to see bullet proof glass install in the collection area with a slide tray. Council asked for estimates. Ms. Sandra Campbell was in the audience and told the council of a problem with dirt bikes riding in the sewer right of way and on Cedarvale Dr. in the afternoons causing a disturbance. We have the engagement letter from Eddie Carrick, PLLC to do our audit for 2022-2023. Julia made a motion to renew the contract with Eddie Carrick. Scotty seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. Julia brought up the white house owned by the town that sits between the Town Hall and the Harmony Library. Julia said we should either sell it or demolish it. Scotty said what would we use it for if we kept it? Doug said it needs quite a bit of work inside. The library uses it for storage. Doug is not sure we could sell it. Buddy has reservations about tearing it down. Julia said we could see if the county would buy it. Buddy suggested that maybe we could table it until the June Meeting . Julia said maybe donate it to the county and let them keep it up. Julia made a motion to table until the June meeting. Buddy seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. Julia reported that there is a sidewalk tripping hazard where the new car wash is going. Mayor Matney said he will have someone look at it. Passing Zone on Hwy 21 North – Vickie Sawyer is working on this for us. ADJOURNMENT: As there was no other business Julia made a motion to adjourn the meeting. Buddy seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. ______________________________ ________________________ Town Clerk Mayor

title: Board of Aldermen Meeting - April 4, 2022
text: ay Town of Harmony 3389 Harmony Hwy, Harmony, NC 28634 704-546-2339 DATE: April 4, 2022 TIME: 4:00 PM ATTENDEES: Lee Matney, Mayor N Sankey Gaither - Council Member Julia Clanton - Council Member Doug Galliher – Council Member Scotty Harris – Council Member AGENDA: Call to Order: Mayor Matney Invocation: Council Member Harris Pledge of Allegiance: Council Member Clanton Approval of minutes: Buddy Gaither made a motion to approve the March 7th minutes. Julia Clanton seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. Julia made a motion to approve the March 7th closed session minutes. Doug seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. Public Comment Period: Each speaker is asked to limit comments to 3 minutes. The total comment period will be 15 minutes or less. Citizens should sign up with the Town Clerk to speak to the board by 3:00 pm on the Thursday prior to the meeting on Monday night. At the time of sign-up speakers should state their subject or the matter of concern Speakers should be the Town Board is interested in hearing the concerns of the speakers, however speakers should not expect Board action or deliberation on the subject matter brought up during the Public Comment segment. Topics requiring further investigation will be referred to the appropriate town officials or staff and may be scheduled for a future agenda. Thank you for your consideration of the Town Council, staff and other speakers. Mayor Matney welcomed the guests, Gene Powers, Priscilla Holmes and Rev. Clyde Parks to the meeting. Melissa Gaither from the Harmony Library presented updates for the library. She said they now have six public computers and will be getting 22 hot spots that can be checked out. They have four chrome books. All programs are doing well. Sean Turner was on the agenda to speak to the Board, but did not show up. Rev. Parks told the group that he is working with Harmony School to hold a 9-week summer Transition Camp for 5th graders going to middle school. They will focus on the I Ready Program (Reading and Math) and help students with struggles. They are only taking 25 kids and are looking for sponsors. They are hoping to get the kids up to grade level. Cost will be $35.00 for 9 weeks and will be only for kids in the Harmony School area. They will work on problem solving, avoiding conflict, bullying, personal hygiene, etc. Gene Powers told the group that he appreciated all they did for the town. Mayor Matney announced the end of the public comment period. OLD BUSINESS: Park Fence – Pine needles have been put around the community building. Mulching has been started along the fence. New screens have been put up at the community building. Mayor Matney told the group that the water fountain at the park is dirty and nasty and asked if anyone had any objections to removing it. All agreed to remove it. Department of Transportation – Mayor Matney told the council that the DOT is suppose to be reducing the speed limits inside the town limits to 35 mph and leading into the town to 45 mph. Scotty suggested that all city streets should have 25 mph street signs. SCIF Grant – $200,000. Was deposited into our account on March 29th. We have examples of formal advertising for bids for paving streets. NCLM – Scotty would like to have Marcus Abernathy from the League meet with us at the May meeting. NEW BUSINESS: 2022 Audit – Clerk talked of Engagement letter from Eddie Carrick, CPA that we need to sign if we want them to do our audit this year. Scotty made a motion to sign the engagement letter. Buddy seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. Clerk presented a resolution from Withers Ravenal that they apply for a grant on behalf of the Town for wastewater treatment. Julia made a motion to sign the resolution. Scotty seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. Mayor Matney told the council that he had spoken with Keith Lentz regarding Love Valley. Some in Love Valley want Keith to resume hauling their wastewater to our sewer facility. Question was asked “Do we want to resume it? They are paying $ .04 per gallon now” Julia is in favor of hauling. Others are in favor also. Keith also told the Mayor about a Bed & Breakfast that opened in Mooresville. Iredell County issued all permits. Now they are telling them that the septic tank is inadequate. Lentz wants to haul to our system. There will be no industrial or commercial waste, only household. Board is very interested in Lentz hauling for them. Sign – Julia would like us to think about a new sign for out front. Scotty wants to think about a new location for sign. Buddy is in favor of a new sign. ADJOURNMENT: As there was no other business Julia made a motion to adjourn the meeting. Doug seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. ______________________________ ________________________ Town Clerk Mayor

title: Board of Aldermen Meeting - April 5, 2021
text: TOWN OF HARMONY MEETING MINUTES Town of Harmony 3389 Harmony Hwy, Harmony, NC 28634 704-546-2339 DATE: April 5, 2021 TIME: 4:00 PM ATTENDEES: Lee Matney, Mayor N Sankey Gaither - Council Member Julia Clanton - Council Member Doug Galliher – Council Member Scotty Harris – Council Member AGENDA: Call to Order: Mayor Matney Invocation: Council Member Harris Pledge of Allegiance: Council Member Clanton Approval of minutes: Julia Clanton made a motion to approve the March 1st minutes. title: Board of Aldermen Meeting - April 7, 2025
text: Town of Harmony 3389 Harmony Hwy, Harmony, NC 28634 704-546-2339_________ DATE: April 7, 2025 TIME: 6:00 PM ATTENDEES: Sean Turner, Mayor Chris Pierce, Council Member Scotty Harris, Council Member Brandon Angell, Council Member Wanda Edwards, Town Clerk / Finance Officer AGENDA: Call to Order: Mayor Turner Invocation: Scotty Harris Pledge of Allegiance: Approval of minutes: Chris Pierce made a motion to approve the March 3rd , 2025 minutes. Brandon Angell seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. Scotty Harris made a motion to approve the minutes of the March 12th meeting. Brandon seconded the motion carried 4-0. Brandon made a motion to approve the minutes of the March 17th meeting. Chris seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. PUBLIC COMMENT PERIOD: Citizens should sign up with the Town Clerk to speak to the board by 3:00 pm on Thursday prior to the meeting on Monday night . Each speaker is asked to limit comments to 3 minutes. The total comment period will be 15 minutes or less. At the time of sign-up, speakers should state their subject or the matter of concern. Speakers should be aware that the Town Board is interested in hearing the concerns of the speakers, however, speakers should not expect Board action or deliberation on the subject matter brought up during the Public Comment segment. Topics requiring further investigation will be referred to the appropriate town officials, or staff and may be scheduled for a future agenda. Thank you for your consideration of the Town Council, staff, and other speakers. Skylar Benge who was scheduled to speak about installing a “blessing box” on town property did not show up for the meeting. OLD BUSINESS: Spring In the Park: Event was very successful. Food vendors did very well. We had a good number of people attend. Farmers Market will begin the 2nd Friday in May. Skinners Food Truck has asked to come back and serve. Information on Farmers Market will be posted on our face book page. COMMUNITY CENTER BATHROOMS: Mayor will call Cory Pennell to get scheduled. PLAYGROUND: We have a quote from KAN Contracts to do 2 deck replacement pieces at the slide and replace current swings with: 1 swing with 2 bays, 2 belt seats and 2 tot seats for a total cost of $8,500.00. They reported that our present swings are too dangerous to repair and they are out of code of code because they are too high. Jared said this is a pressing issue. Mulch will need to be redone at the swing and the border may need adjusting. Chris made a motion to approve the contract with KAN Contracts as stated. Jared seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. Tim and Doug will dismantle the old swing at the appropriate time. Clerk presented an engagement letter from Tony Brewer, CPA, PC to conduct the 2025 audit for the town. Scotty made a motion to approve Tony to conduct the audit. Brandon seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. NEW BUSINESS: Hebron Baptist Church youth are looking to help elderly. Chris has a great aunt – suggested Ms. Rankin Highland Pt. Ave. Quotes for WWTP grant funding – Mayor wants to work with Jeff to do one/two projects at a time Street Lights on Cedarvale (3) Paving completed at curve on Highland Pt. Ave. Do away with speed bumps on John Deere – get quote for speed plane Maintenance log for equipment Lentz and John Gritt – discussed dumping – question asked “is there a way we can measure how many they bring or do we just trust them?” They call into office each time they dump and report number of gallons dumped. Republic wants to bring waste from porta-jons. Problem is we won’t know what we are getting. Lentz and Gritt are now dumping at manhole in front of old café building. Mayor wants to plan a day long planning retreat for sometime this fall. Helena funds are frozen for review. Need to discuss sewer rates: in town rates – out of town rates – commercial hook-up rate. Chris said we need to raise rates. Waiting for McGill to get back to us with rate study. As there was no other business, Chris made a motion to adjourn. Scotty seconded. Motion carried 4-0. _____________________________________ _________________________________ Wanda Edwards, Town Clerk Sean Turner, Mayor

title: Board of Aldermen Meeting - April 8, 2024
text: Town of Harmony 3389 Harmony Hwy, Harmony, NC 28634 704-546-2339 DATE: April 8, 2024 TIME: 4:00 PM ATTENDEES: Sean Turner, Mayor Chris Pierce - Council Member Scotty Harris - Council Member Jared Clark – Council Member Brandon Angell – Council Member Wanda Edwards – Town Clerk AGENDA: Call to Order: Mayor Turner Invocation: Council Member: Scotty Harris Pledge of Allegiance: Approval of minutes: Scotty Harris made a motion to approve the March 4th , 2024 minutes. Brandon Angel seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. Scotty made a motion to approve the March 25th, 2024 minutes. Jared Clark seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. Public Comment Period: Each speaker is asked to limit comments to 3 minutes. The total comment period will be 15 minutes or less. Citizens should sign up with the Town Clerk to speak to the board by 3:00 pm on the Thursday prior to the meeting on Monday night. At the time of sign-up speakers should state their subject or the matter of concern Speakers should be the Town Board is interested in hearing the concerns of the speakers, however speakers should not expect Board action or deliberation on the subject matter brought up during the Public Comment segment. Topics requiring further investigation will be referred to the appropriate town officials or staff and may be scheduled for a future agenda. Thank you for your consideration of the Town Council, staff and other speakers. Melissa Gaither from the Harmony Library spoke to the group and told that Kevin Campbell will be at the library on April 27th at 2 p.m. to talk about the benefits of incorporating native plants into landscapes. World Outlook will also be doing special programs for senior citizens during May, June, July and August. PUBLIC HEARING: ORDINANCE – ARTICLE 5 – SECTION 2.80 - ZONING BOARD -This ordinance speaks about who should serve on the Zoning Board and says that the board shall consist of 5 members appointed by the Mayor and Board of Aldermen. On April 3, 2018 the Board voted to amend this ordinance to read that the Zoning Board of Adjustments consists of 5 members of the Town Council and the Mayor. The Council at this time wishes to amend the ordinance to once again read that the 5 members of the Zoning Board be appointed by the Mayor and Town Council. As there was no one in the audience to speak for or against this change - Jared made a motion that the 5 members of the Zoning Board be appointed by the Mayor and Town Council. Brandon seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. OLD BUSINESS: FARMERS MARKET: We will hold our Farmer’s Market the 2nd Friday of each month beginning in May through October. Our first Farmer’s Market will be held on May 10th from 4 – 7 PM. Doug Galliher is the market manager. We have home made ice cream and 67 Pizza scheduled to be here. Clay Lunsford will provide the music. Mayor asked for names of anyone that we should send an invitation. MURAL ON SIDE OF BUILDING: Mayor Turner told the group that Ernie Johnson from Print Path puts pictures directly on the wall. This may be something to consider rather than having a mural painted. WEB SITE: Grant wants to meet with some of the local people who are older and have lived in Harmony for many years. He wants to find out some of the history of the Town to help him with the branding for the Town. Mayor Turner told the group that Grant has told him someone to manage the website and the social media would run between $700.00 - $1200.00 per month. All agreed that was too much. Mayor Turner knows someone who may be interested in doing it for less. He will reach out to him. NEW BUSINESS: SEWER PLANTS: The by-pass has been completed at the Little Wilkesboro and Linda Dr. lift stations. The trees at Little Wilkesboro need to be taken down. Ben Shelton and the Youth from Hebron Baptist Church will be out in the community doing volunteer work. Priscilla Holmes suggested contacting the Council on Aging to see if they knew of anyone who might be in need of help. 4-H: Priscilla has helped find two volunteers to work with 4-H. GRASS LOT BEHIND COMMUNITY BUILDING: Mayor Turner has contacted Joe Binkley about spraying to get rid of the weeds. Mayor suggested using the field for the Tractor Show on May 18th. He suggested that we may be able to rent out the field for future events. Interest has been expressed about having an equipment auction there in the future. There will be a cruise-in on April 20th to benefit Kathy Shoemaker. TELEMETRY: Installation began today. TOMLIN MILL RD.: Mayor Turner has learned from Matthew Todd that we cannot annex out farther than three miles from the town limits. We need an agreement with the City of Statesville to set jurisdiction limits as to how far out they can come. Mayor Turner thinks we should pursue getting service at Tomlin Mill Rd. area because it is closer to our plant than Union Grove area. We would be able to set a double rate for sewer. Circle K is also supposedly coming to Tomlin Mill Rd. Discussed a standalone system Aqua Tech which treat 25, 000 gallons for a cost of $250,000.00. A lift station alone without lines, etc. would cost $250,000.00. The standalone system treats water or we can do sub-surface irrigation. We could get grant money to run lines at a later date. Golden Leaf provides funds for extending sewer, grading or infrastructure. A standalone system will last a good long while. SEWER RATES: Discussed sewer rates for those on sewer who are outside the city limits. We could double the rate or have them self-annex. The town own 57 acres of land at the Waste Water Treatment Plant that is not inside of the city limits. Mayor will discuss with Matthew Todd and Town Attorney, Kathy Dixon the advantages of annexing into the city limits. PIPE ON LINDA DR.: Work has not been started NORTH CAROLINA CAPITAL TRUST MANAGEMENT: First Bank is paying 3.1% on the Money Market. Mayor asked “do you want to move money from First Horizon to First Bank until the CD at First Horizon matures in September and then put it all in the NCCTM?” Brandon made a motion that we move the money. Jared seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. Scotty wants to see if we can get a “No Passing” zone in front of his house. Need to think about installing a red light at Grose Street. Mayor said we need to do a Saturday all day retreat for planning. ADJOURNMENT: As there was no other business: Jared made a motion to adjourn. Brandon seconded the motion. Motion carried 3-0. ______________________________ ________________________ Town Clerk Mayor

title: Board of Aldermen Meeting - August 1, 2022
text: Town of Harmony 3389 Harmony Hwy, Harmony, NC 28634 704-546-2339 DATE: August 1, 2022 TIME: 4:00 PM ATTENDEES: Lee Matney, Mayor N Sankey Gaither - Council Member Julia Clanton - Council Member Doug Galliher – Council Member Scotty Harris – Council Member AGENDA: Call to Order: Mayor Matney Invocation: Council Member Harris Pledge of Allegiance: Council Member Clanton Approval of minutes: Scotty Harris made a motion to approve the July 11th minutes. Doug Galliher seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. Julia Clanton made a motion to approve the July 22nd minutes. Scotty seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. Public Comment Period: Each speaker is asked to limit comments to 3 minutes. The total comment period will be 15 minutes or less. Citizens should sign up with the Town Clerk to speak to the board by 3:00 pm on the Thursday prior to the meeting on Monday night. At the time of sign-up speakers should state their subject or the matter of concern Speakers should be the Town Board is interested in hearing the concerns of the speakers, however speakers should not expect Board action or deliberation on the subject matter brought up during the Public Comment segment. Topics requiring further investigation will be referred to the appropriate town officials or staff and may be scheduled for a future agenda. Thank you for your consideration of the Town Council, staff and other speakers. Mayor Matney welcomed the guests to the meeting. Mr. and Mrs. Canalis who live at 3595 Harmony Hwy spoke to the council about the disrepair of the property belonging to Remi Lavoi at 3589 Harmony Hwy. They spoke of the rats and snakes coming from the property. A tree from the Lavoi property fell on their carport resulting in $700.00 worth of damage. They want him held accountable for the damage. Mrs. Pierce from 130 Gristmill Lane, also a neighbor of the Lavoi property, spoke of the weeds and thornbushes that are growing on the property. She was told that the town attorney had sent him several letters to no avail. They were told to call Jeff Blood at Iredell County Solid Waste or Susan Robertson to see if they could help them. Ray Ruppe from Creative Signs presented a proposal to install an electrical message sign at the town hall. His cost for the sign and installation is $28,130.09. Julia asked how long the sign should last and Ray said between 25-30 years, but we may have to replace a module sometime. Cost for the module will be about $300.00 plus $100.00 for installation. They provide a one year warranty on everything and after that 2 year on parts. They are out 6-8 weeks to get work done. Mayor Matney closed the meeting for public comment. OLD BUSINESS: Fence Line at WWTP – Scotty went with Charles Trivette to look at dead trees and weeds that need to be cleared off the fence line. Jeff said if all trees were removed it would increase noise from blowers and we would get more noise complaints from residents living close by the plant. Scotty made a motion to have Charles do the work. Buddy seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. Upstairs – Question was brought up – could we remove a window upstairs and replace it with a door. Mr. Troyer submitted a cost estimate of $1,335.00 to install remove window and install a door upstairs to make it more accessible for Mr. Cass when he needs to work on the camera on the roof that face the bank. After discussion, Buddy said he thinks it is a bad idea. Matter was tabled for another bid. Associated Metals Works, Inc. has submitted a bid of $2,132.44 to furnish and install handrail, where the side walk ends and turns 90 degrees towards Fast Phils service station. Mayor Matney asked them to wait to make a decision until he checked with Associated Metals to be sure the sidewalk handrail meets the ADA specifications. Harmony School Fence – After discussion regarding ownership of the fence, we will have Ms. Dixon contact the Iredell County School Board to see if they claim ownership of the fence. If not, she will send a letter to property owners bordering the fence (Mr. & Mrs. Luther Lawson, Gary Feimster and Dale Hague) to see if any of them claim ownership of the fence. In the meeting on July 22, 2022 Scotty made a motion to rescind the property tax increase that had been set at the June 21st meeting. We were not able to rescind this tax because tax bills had already been sent to the printer. At the July 22, 2022 meeting Julia made a motion to increase the sewer rates by $1.55 – motion was seconded by Scotty and passed 4-0. After working with Joe Haney during audit preparation, Joe suggested that we not pass along the sewer increase the same year we increase property tax. Buddy made a motion to rescind the sewer increase. Julia seconded the motion. Motion carried 47-0. NEW BUSINESS: ADJOURNMENT: As there was no other business Julia made a motion to adjourn the meeting. Scotty seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. ______________________________ ________________________ Town Clerk Mayor

title: Board of Aldermen Meeting - August 12, 2019
text: Town of Harmony Meeting Minutes Town of Harmony North Carolina 3389 Harmony Highway, Harmony, NC 28634 704-546-2339 DATE: August 12, 2019 TIME: 7:00 PM ATTENDEES: Lee Matney, Mayor John Ray Campbell – Alderman Julia Clanton – Alderman Doug Galliher – Alderman Scotty Harris - Alderman AGENDA: Call to Order: Mayor Matney Invocation: Alderman Campbell Pledge of Allegiance: Alderman Clanton Approval of previous Months Minutes Julia Clanton made a motion to approve the minutes July 1, 2019 regular meeting and the July 1st special meeting (pay raise for Tim Trivette). Doug Galliher seconded the motion. Motion carried. Public Comment Period: Notes on the Comment Period Each speaker is asked to limit comments to 3 minutes. The total comment period will be 15 minutes or less. Citizens should sign up with the Town Clerk to speak to the board by 3:00pm on the Thursday prior to the meeting on Monday night. At the time of sign-up, speakers should state their subject or the matter of concern. Speakers should be aware the Town Board is interested in hearing the concerns of the speakers; however speakers should not expect Board action or deliberation on the subject matter brought up during the Public Comment segment. Topics requiring further investigation will be referred to the appropriate town officials or staff and may be scheduled for a future agenda. Thank you for your consideration of the Town Council, staff, and other speakers. . Council welcomed Matthew Todd and Matthew Pierce from Iredell County to speak to the group about erosion control. Matthew Pierce spoke to the group about the need for erosion control. He gave the council a copy of a resolution that he is asking the town board to sign. The resolution would allow the town to come under county erosion regulations. Erosion control is for 1 acre or less. Erosion control must begin no later than 14 days after grading begins. If we are under the State the cost for the inspection is $75.00 – under the county the cost would be $175.00 per acre (fraction of an acre is rounded up). The county cost is higher because of a quicker turn around than with the state and also the county can monitor the project closer. Turn around inspection with the county would be 5-14 days. They need the town’s decision back within a month. Council will make a decision at the September 9th meeting. Melissa Gaither from the Iredell County Library thanked the town board for the support over the years. She said the library was busy with the summer reading program this summer and discussed upcoming projects. Old Business: Speed Bumps – Mayor reported that we have had some complaints about the speed bumps. If we ever do any more, we should be sure the sign goes up before the speed bumps are installed. Julia said it has slowed and reduced traffic. Grose Street has been paved. They have been back and addressed the bump at some of the driveways and dressed the sides of the road. Road Market – People seemed pleased with the 3 day market. Suggestions for next year were: maybe we could bring in old cars for a car show; more face book posts and maybe a better place to put the vendors. Suggestion was made that maybe we could use the lot across from the Baptist Church on Little Wilkesboro Road. The town could rent out the lots and split the money with the church. Porta jons could be placed in the parking lot at the church and at the Family Dollar. Harmony Hill Camp Meeting – The churches are coming together to hold the meeting on the land owned by Ben Shelton on Hwy 21 and put up a tent. Sewer Right of Way has been cleared. Charge was $300.00. Tommy’s Lawn Care will bush hog this area once a month and weed eat around the man holes. Abandoned, Junked and Nuisance Vehicles Ordinance – Wording of ordinance was approved by town attorney. Scotty made a motion to adopt the ordinance with the exception of adding the words “No abandoned, junked or nuisance vehicles in any yard that is visible from the street.” Julia Clanton seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. Wording will be added and ordinance will be added to the existing town ordinances. New Business Census – Town has received a letter from Beth Jones, County Manager, asking that we appoint a staff person or elected individual to serve on a Complete Count Committee. Before anyone agreed to serve, they wanted to know more about what would be expected from that person. Waste Water Treatment Plant Road – We have received a bid from County Boy Landscaping for repairs to the road in the amount of $17,226.75. Scotty will get a bid from Charles Trivette before a decision is made. Town Hall Roof – the roof is leaking over the dining area. We will get a bid from Garcia Roofing, Dry-Tech Roofing and Adam Ledbetter. Repair needs to be made as soon as possible. Love Valley – Mayor reported that they are only doing a pumping about every six weeks. If waiting this long puts us out of compliance with state, we will drop them. State Sewer Inspection has been completed. Only a couple of minor things were noted. Overall inspection was good. Interim Town Clerk – Town Clerk will be out of work for about 3 weeks in October due to surgery. Town Board was asked to appoint Doug Galliher as Interim Town Clerk during this period. John Ray Campbell asked if this would not be a conflict of interest. Scotty Harris made a motion to approve the request after checking with town attorney to see if this would constitute a conflict of interest. Julia Clanton seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. Julia also brought up some thoughts for consideration: painting a mural on side of Town Hall (maybe the Town seal); and replacing the information sign. Scotty also told the group that someone has cows inside the city limits close to his house. The pasture next to Sue Lawson’s home needs to be tended. Also there is a horse in the pasture that may need animal control to check. Jimmy Reavis has bought the “Neighborhood Grill” property on Grose Street and is planning to open a restaurant. Adjournment Julia made a motion to adjourn. John Ray seconded. Motion carried. Town Clerk___________________________________Mayor____________________________

title: Board of Aldermen Meeting - August 2, 2021
text: TOWN OF HARMONY MEETING MINUTES Town of Harmony 3389 Harmony Hwy, Harmony, NC 28634 704-546-2339 DATE: August 2, 2021 TIME: 4:00 PM ATTENDEES: Lee Matney, Mayor N Sankey Gaither - Council Member Julia Clanton - Council Member Doug Galliher – Council Member Scotty Harris – Council Member AGENDA: Call to Order: Mayor Matney Invocation: Council Member Harris Pledge of Allegiance: Council Member Clanton Approval of minutes: Julia Clanton made a motion to approve the July 12th minutes. Doug Galliher seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. Public Comment Period: Each speaker is asked to limit comments to 3 minutes. The total comment period will be 15 minutes or less. Citizens should sign up with the Town Clerk to speak to the board by 3:00 pm on the Thursday prior to the meeting on Monday night. At the time of sign-up speakers should state their subject or the matter of concern Speakers should be the Town Board is interested in hearing the concerns of the speakers, however speakers should not expect Board action or deliberation on the subject matter brought up during the Public Comment segment. Topics requiring further investigation will be referred to the appropriate town officials or staff and may be scheduled for a future agenda. Thank you for your consideration of the Town Council, staff and other speakers. Shawn Turner spoke to the council. He has spoken with Wes Bell who is the engineer who helped with the building of our sewer system. Wes told Shawn that he could not tap in up at the community center as he had previously discussed doing because of the elevation from his house to the manhole. The best manhole gravity feed is across the park parking lot to the manhole by the porta-jon. There is a strip of unclaimed land behind his house. He is working with the county to see if he can get this land. If so, he could put his septic tank drainage field back there. He is going to put a well on the side of his house next to the field that the town leases to Gene Powers. Shawn says if his well goes there, no kind of spraying for crops, etc. can be done close to the well. He will want to lease the land himself. He also asked that we provide him with a copy of the July minutes and a letter stating that we do not provide sewer on Woodland Bend and Tomlinson Ave. He told the group that as of this date he has moved cattle onto the pastureland he owns on Tomlinson Ave. He is bringing in a bucket truck to get rid of a big tree next to the fence at the park for Chris Pierce. He also told the council that he would like to plant trees along Woodland Bend to match those he has planted on his property. Lane Harrell, Project Manager with Clayton Homes and Shay Connor wanted to speak to the council about rezoning a parcel of land at 165 Cedarvale Dr. that she has purchased through Clayton Homes and wants to set up a double wide mobile home on the lot. That land is inside the city limits and is currently zoned for site built or modular homes. Lee told the council that if they decide to rezone this property, they can rezone only this one piece of property and not the entire area. Julia said that for now we should only consider this one piece of property. Buddy agreed with Julia. Council members want to drive out there and see what the area looks like. Will meet on Wednesday, August 4th at 3:30 pm to make a decision about the rezoning. OLD BUSINESS: Ms. Dixon’s report on results of letters to property owners – 118 Tomlinson Ave. Mr. Partin is working to resolve these issues. Chris Harris is interested in purchasing the property and will see that it is cleaned up. Luther Moore’s property – he is sending a representative up here to look at the property. He stated that he would look at the report and get back to Ms. Dixon. He did indicate that it was likely that all of the property would be sold. Julia asked the Mayor to direct Ms. Dixon to call Mr. Moore back. Remi Lavoi – wants an extension on his ten-day deadline to get his property cleaned up. Mayor Matney wants Ms. Dixon to stay after him. Lawson property – some mowing of the pasture has been done. Council wants Ms. Dixon to send Mrs. Lawson a second letter about continuing the mowing of the pasture. Fencing at the park – Mayor reported that the surveying will cost between $500. - $1,000. Marty Cline will only mark corners. Marty recommends that we go ahead and remove the privacy fence before he does the survey. Scotty said not to wait 6—8 month before we put up a new fence. Marty said he would be able to do the survey the second or third week in August. Mayor Matney suggested just doing the back section of the fence for now. (Consensus of the council is that none want a chain link fence) Julia suggested that we either go back with what we have or go with the kind of fencing that is around the cemetery. Julia said to leave the existing privacy fence up, have it surveyed and go ahead and secure the materials for a new fence so there will be no delay in getting a new fence put back up. Ad for ORC – 2 people have responded to the ad. They seem to be very interested in the job. Rate Study - Tyson Edwards from Rural Water has sent the information to Troy Cassidy. Troy is going to look at it and present his recommendations to the council. Town Clerk presented a quote from Dry-Tech Commercial Roofing to replace the deteriorated roof on the front part of the Town Hall. The amount of the quote was $19,622.00. Board asked that we get more quotes to compare prices. Asked Statesville Roofing for a quote. They could not quote because they cannot get materials. Ostwalt Roofing came out and looked at the roof, we have not heard back from them. Fence – School Road – Harmony School does not own this fence. Johnn Cook with the DOT is trying to find the encroachment for the fence being put up. Tim and Doug have replaced some of the bad rails. NEW BUSINESS: Audit – Tony Brewer will be here August 4th and 5th to do the audit for 2020-2021. Town Meeting for September will be held at 4 pm on the 13th due to the 6th being a holiday Mayor asked if council thought COVID cleaning should be continued after each rental at the Community Center. After discussion, Julia said that she thought we should continue as we are now for another month and after that review month to month. Julie wants to see the town web site active and kept up to date. Town Clerk will talk with Cole Cass to see if he can help us with this. ADJOURNMENT: As there was no other business, Julia made a motion to adjourn the meeting. Buddy seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. ______________________________ ________________________ Town Clerk Mayor

title: Board of Aldermen Meeting - August 4, 2025
text: Town of Harmony 3389 Harmony Hwy, Harmony, NC 28634 704-546-2339_________ DATE: August 4, 2025 TIME: 6:00 PM ATTENDEES: Sean Turner, Mayor Chris Pierce, Council Member Scotty Harris, Council Member Brandon Angell, Council Member Wanda Edwards, Town Clerk / Finance Officer Call to Order: Mayor Turner Invocation: Mayor Turner Pledge of Allegiance: Welcome by Mayor AGENDA: Scotty Harris made a motion to approve tonight’s agenda. Brandon Angell seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. Chris Pierce made a made a motion to approve the minutes of the July 7th meeting. Jared seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. Brandon made a motion to approve the minutes of the July 17th, 2025 meeting. Jared seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. Jared made a motion to approve the July 31st meeting. Brandon seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. PUBLIC COMMENT PERIOD: Citizens should sign up with the Town Clerk to speak to the board by 3:00 pm on Thursday prior to the meeting on Monday night . Each speaker is asked to limit comments to 3 minutes. The total comment period will be 15 minutes or less. At the time of sign-up, speakers should state their subject or the matter of concern. Speakers should be aware that the Town Board is interested in hearing the concerns of the speakers, however, speakers should not expect Board action or deliberation on the subject matter brought up during the Public Comment segment. Topics requiring further investigation will be referred to the appropriate town officials, or staff and may be scheduled for a future agenda. Thank you for your consideration of the Town Council, staff, and other speakers. Doug Galliher reported on the Farmer’s Marker. Few vendors. Next year he wants our Farmer’s Market to have its’ own Facebook page. Also said we need different food vendors. Fall Festival will be held on 10/04/2025 at the park. Melissa Gaither from the Harmony Library reported that the 8 week Summer Reading Program was a success. Talked to council about the Story Walk and that we might want to do that at the park. Kasia Thompson from Centralina Regional Council spoke to the group about joining the group and the benefits they have that could be of help to us. Fees are on a case by case basis based on time to complete project. Mayor said they could help with the retreat he is wanting to have. Jared asked if they keep a record of good engineering firms? She said they probably do. They have lots of resources. We can have one delegate for their meeting. Need to appoint an alternate delegate also. OLD BUSINESS: Speed table – Mayor read new proposed quote from Mathis paving to remove 2 speed bumps on John Deere Dr. and install one speed table. New price is $6,600.00. Scotty made a motion to proceed with replacing the speed bumps with a speed table at a cost of $6,600.00. Chris seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. JENNINGS PARK: Contract is up, “Do we want to continue as we are doing now?” All agreed to continue letting them dump from Jennings Park into our sewer. CENTRALINA REGIONAL COUNCIL: Clerk read a Resolution For Membership in Centralina Regional Council. Scotty made a motion that we sign the resolution and become a member of the Council upon approval from them. Jared seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. Jared made a motion to pay the $142.00 fee. Chris seconded. Motion carried 4-0. JEFF JONES: Reporting on progress of grant funds – waiting on quotes from Associated Metals and Johnson Utility and Grading. He gave them a deadline of 8-6-2025 to get the quotes to him in order to be considered. He said blowers are a good portion of the grant money. Associated Metals has a copy of our specs. High ammonia in May – Lentz and Gritt dumped within a few days of hit. Jeff thinks this is when we got hit. One week was a large violation. Brandon asked “how was high ammonia missed?” Jared asked, “Can we ask for samples they are dumping?” NEW BUSINESS: WEB-SITE UPDATE: Janet Harriman, Copper Gate Media spoke to the group. She presented potential invoice for August and September at $1125.00 per month. Mayor asked, “ how much after September?”. Mayor said website from Grypos is not hard, folders are there, just need content added. Janet’s concern is adding content to spaces at Grypos. Said this is very difficult – without control of structure, she is concerned. ZONING BOARD: Will meet the 3rd week of each month. They can decide what day of the week. Grypos: Mayor has talked with Jeremy about separating from them – host, billing (host no problem – need 2-3 days) Mayor is to meet with Jeremy. Chris made a motion to go Jeremy and not pay any more. Jared seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. BUILD AND SERVE: After discussion, Jared made a motion that the Town hire Build and Serve for Phase 1 (Core Project Scope & Deliverables). Brandon seconded the motion . Motion carried 3-0. Scotty Harris did not vote for or against the project. SEWER RATES: Hole a public hearing 8/18/2025 at 6 pm – proposed increase – inside city 1.5% - outside city limits 1.5 times bill. As there was no other business, Chris made a motion to adjourn. Scotty seconded. Motion carried 4-0. _____________________________________ _________________________________ Wanda Edwards, Town Clerk Sean Turner, Mayor

title: Board of Aldermen Meeting - August 5, 2024
text: Town of Harmony 3389 Harmony Hwy, Harmony, NC 28634 704-546-2339 DATE: August 5, 2024 TIME: 6:00 PM ATTENDEES: Sean Turner, Mayor Chris Pierce - Council Member Scotty Harris - Council Member Jared Clark – Council Member Brandon Angell – Council Member Wanda Edwards – Town Clerk Guests: Russell Byrd and Jeff Jones AGENDA: Call to Order: Mayor Turner Invocation: Mayor Sean Turner Pledge of Allegiance: Approval of minutes: Brandon Angell made a motion to approve the July 1st, 2024 minutes. Scotty Harris seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. Chris Pierce made a motion to approve the July 15th minutes. Brandon seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. Public Comment Period: Each speaker is asked to limit comments to 3 minutes. The total comment period will be 15 minutes or less. Citizens should sign up with the Town Clerk to speak to the board by 3:00 pm on the Thursday prior to the meeting on Monday night. At the time of sign-up speakers should state their subject or the matter of concern Speakers should be the Town Board is interested in hearing the concerns of the speakers, however speakers should not expect Board action or deliberation on the subject matter brought up during the Public Comment segment. Topics requiring further investigation will be referred to the appropriate town officials or staff and may be scheduled for a future agenda. Thank you for your consideration of the Town Council, staff, and other speakers. Jeff introduced Russell Byrd from McGill Associates, the firm managing our Assets and Inventory Assessment grant. Regarding concerns that there has been no activity or communication from McGill in regards to any progress of this grant, Russell told the group that Jared Wright had left the company and he had inherited the job the first of May. He discussed a survey (map) done by West Consultants. Problems per Jeff are I&I. Water can go in through manholes, clean—outs, and pipe joints. He has met with representative from KRG and they can help locate I&I. They think we are getting water in from multiple sources. We do not have a quote from them yet as to what their services will cost. Possibly we can use funds designated for mapping to do the I&I. Russell will share this contact and see if he can get DEQ to approve. He has applied for funds for equipment renewal. Scotty said that Linda and Gaither are top priority pump stations. Manhole top, clean-out is probably where water is coming from. Linda is fed by outfall from a stream. Russell wants to get KRG to come and look at some of the areas where they think problems are. Mapping will help find trouble spots. If we can’t put in rain stoppers, we can use vents or raise clean-outs. Question was asked if we know anything about the other grant money. No word yet as to when we will get it. Jared asked Jeff to see the run times for June. Sean answered “not tonight.” Russell likes the idea of comparing dry time to future rain/flooding we are expecting. Jared says it will save time and money to do some of the investigation ourself. Russell said we need to exercise pumps so they don’t go septic. Russell told the group that with the amount of state money being applied for, lots are not getting funded. One out of every four do not get funded. OLD BUSINESS: COMMUNITY CENTER BATHROOMS: Mayor Turner will meet with Laura Elliott to see if Community Center Board will pay for half of the bathroom repairs. CAMERAS AT WWTP: Waiting for cameras to come in. TWO MEETINGS PER MONTH: Decided to have one meeting per month and have a special meeting if something comes up that needs to be discussed. WEB SITE: Will have a special meeting in August for update. FARMERS MARKET: Postponed until 8/16/2024 due to forecasted rain. STAGE: We have received the stage. We need to decide on a rental price if someone wants to rent it. If rented, Doug and Tim must do set-up and break-down. May want to purchase a trailer to haul it. NEW BUSINESS: FALL FESTIVAL: Clint Vanhoy gave the group some ideas of what to consider when planning the festival. He suggested that we have it on a weekend night and make it a charity event the first year. We need food and games. Suggested we have several food trucks. Mayor Turner has some ideas of who he would like to head up the festival and some he would like to serve on the committee. We need a backup date. Need event coverage insurance. Decided to hold the event on the first Saturday in November. Brandon made a motion to make this an annual event. Chris seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. TRASH CONTRACTS: Waiting for proposals from N. Iredell Sanitation, Republic Services, and North Lake. GOLDEN LEAF: Our proposal for extending sewer line to Love’s and Lowe’s at Tomlin Mill exit has been sent to Iredell County Manager, Beth Mull. ADJOURNMENT: As there was no other business: Scotty made a motion to adjourn. Jared seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. ______________________________ ________________________ Town Clerk Mayor

title: Board of Aldermen Meeting - August 7, 2023
text: Town of Harmony 3389 Harmony Hwy, Harmony, NC 28634 704-546-2339 DATE: August 7, 2023 TIME: 4:00 PM ATTENDEES: Lee Matney, Mayor N Sankey Gaither - Council Member Julia Clanton - Council Member Doug Galliher – Council Member Scotty Harris – Council Member Wanda Edwards – Town Clerk AGENDA: Call to Order: Mayor Matney Invocation: Council Member Harris Pledge of Allegiance: Council Member Clanton Approval of minutes: Scotty Harris made a motion to approve the July 10th minutes. Doug Galliher seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. Doug made a motion to approve the July 17th minutes. Julia Clanton seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. Public Comment Period: Each speaker is asked to limit comments to 3 minutes. The total comment period will be 15 minutes or less. Citizens should sign up with the Town Clerk to speak to the board by 3:00 pm on the Thursday prior to the meeting on Monday night. At the time of sign-up speakers should state their subject or the matter of concern Speakers should be the Town Board is interested in hearing the concerns of the speakers, however speakers should not expect Board action or deliberation on the subject matter brought up during the Public Comment segment. Topics requiring further investigation will be referred to the appropriate town officials or staff and may be scheduled for a future agenda. Thank you for your consideration of the Town Council, staff and other speakers. Elizabeth Hannis from 174 Hayes St. spoke to the group about problems she is having with her sewer. It is backing up. She has had her broken pipe repaired but the problem is not solved. She says that the water from her house has to run up hill to get out to the main sewer line. Jeff told Ms. Hannis that the town’s system is installed properly and whoever installed the line to her home did not account for the grade. She should have had a pump installed at the time it was installed and the county inspector should not have passed inspection on the installation. She said the pump would cost $3,500 plus the cost of installation. She asked the town for help. The town cannot help her monetarily. She has asked Iredell County for the name of the inspector, but was told that they switched to a new computer system and now they do not have that information. Melissa Gaither from the Harmony Library told the group that the Summer Reading Program will end soon. She said the program was a success this year and the numbers were up from last year. H OLD BUSINESS: Cemetery Fence: Fence area has been sprayed to kill weed growth. NEW BUSINESS: Haney CPA: Clerk presented an Engagement letter from Joe Haney to serve as the Town CPA from July 1, 2023 through June 30, 2024. Julia made a motion to keep Joe as the Town’s CPA. Scotty seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. Land Lease: Discussion was brought up about the land the town leases beside the community center. It was proposed that we discontinue leasing the land when the current lease expires in April, 2024. We will notify the current leaser that we will not renew his lease. We need extra parking space for the community center and we could use a portion of this land for addition parking. Julia made a motion to discontinue leasing the land at the expiration of the current lease. Scotty seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. Harmony Night Out: We are working with Pastors Chris Lakey and Clyde Parks to have the Harmony Night Out on October 3rd from 4-6 p.m. Rain date – October 10th. Money Market : Clerk asked for permission to move $200,000.00 out of the General Fund into a new Money Market. Money Market is paying 2.15% interest. We get no interest on monies in the General Fund. Julia made a motion to move the money. Scotty seconded the motion. Motion carried 3-0. Buddy voted “present.” ADJOURNMENT: As there was no other business Doug made a motion to adjourn the meeting. Julia seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. ______________________________ ________________________ Town Clerk Mayor

title: Board of Aldermen Meeting - December 2, 2024
text: Town of Harmony 3389 Harmony Hwy, Harmony, NC 28634 704-546-2339 DATE: December 2, 2024 TIME: 6:00 PM ATTENDEES: Sean Turner, Mayor Chris Pierce - Council Member Scotty Harris - Council Member Jared Clark – Council Member Brandon Angell – Council Member Wanda Edwards – Town Clerk AGENDA: Call to Order: Mayor Turner Invocation: Scotty Harris Pledge of Allegiance: Jared Clark was absent from the meeting. title: Board of Aldermen Meeting - December 3, 2018
text: Town of Harmony Meeting Minutes Town of Harmony North Carolina 3389 Harmony Highway, Harmony, NC 28634 704-546-2339 DATE: December 3, 2018 TIME: 7:00 PM ATTENDEES: Lee Matney, Mayor John Ray Campbell – Alderman Julia Clanton – Alderman Doug Galliher – Alderman Scotty Harris - Alderman AGENDA: Call to Order: Mayor Matney Invocation: Alderman Campbell Pledge of Allegiance: Alderman Clanton Approval of previous Months Minutes Julia Clanton made a motion to approve the November 5th minutes, Scotty Harris seconded. Motion carried. Public Comment Period: Notes on the Comment Period Each speaker is asked to limit comments to 3 minutes. The total comment period will be 15 minutes or less. Citizens should sign up with the Town Clerk to speak to the board by 3:00pm on the Thursday prior to the meeting on Monday night. At the time of sign-up, speakers should state their subject or the matter of concern. Speakers should be aware the Town Board is interested in hearing the concerns of the speakers; however speakers should not expect Board action or deliberation on the subject matter brought up during the Public Comment segment. Topics requiring further investigation will be referred to the appropriate town officials or staff and may be scheduled for a future agenda. Thank you for your consideration of the Town Council, staff, and other speakers. Elizabeth Hannis who lives at 174 Hayes Street in Harmony spoke to the board about cows belonging to Gene Powers causing damage to her yard and property. She wanted the town to do something about the cows. Julia explained to Ms. Hannis that there was nothing the town could do because our ordinances do not apply because Mr. Powers’ farm is not in the town limits. Owner of the cows is liable for the damage and not the town. She was advised to seek the advice of an attorney. Melissa Gaither – Branch Manager of the Harmony Library spoke to the council about the programs the library offers to children and adults. She told the group that funding for these programs and the summer reading program comes from the book sales and they get $300.00 from the county for the summer reading program. She asked the council to help support the summer reading program with a grant of $500.00, but said anything the town could give would be appreciated. Tommy Thompson and Jeremy Thompson of Tommy’s Lawn Care told the council that his contract with the town expires in February 28, 2019. He anticipates no cost increase. He would like to continue to do the mowing for the town. He told the council that if the town puts the mowing out for bids, he would like the opportunity to submit a bid. He also told the council that he picks up trash along the streets, etc at no additional cost to the town and asked if they get bids from others to ask them to include the trash pick- up in their bid. John Ray asked Tommy to write up another bid for mowing. Tommy agreed and said he would have the bid to us before the January meeting. Old Business: Jake Brake Ordinance – Mayor Matney told the group that notices regarding the “Jake Brake” ordinance had been posted for public notice. He asked Julia Clanton to read aloud the proposed ordinance so the audience would know what the ordinance states. Julia Clanton made a motion to implement the “Jake Brake” ordinance into the Town Ordinances. Scotty Harris seconded the motion. Motion carried 4 in favor 0 against. Repairs to the pavement on Dogwood Forest Loop have been completed in a satisfactory manner. Snow removal – Country Boy Landscaping submitted a bid of $3,000.00 for removing snow from designated streets within the town limits of Harmony and Charles Trivette submitted a bid of $2,000.00. The contract the town has with Charles Trivette expires on December 21, 2018. Julia stated that the town has been pleased with work performed by Country Boy in the past. Charles Trivette has told the May that he is capable and has the equipment to do the job. Doug Galliher suggested to the group that they need to look at the two bids more and discuss again in a few days. Julia Clanton told the group that the full time Town Clerk position needs to be decided upon by January 1st, 2019. Lee suggested that council discuss this at a later time. New Business: Matthew Todd and Leslie Meadows were present to discuss the rezoning of the Lowry property located on Highway 21 south. Leslie gave a description of the property annexed on November 5th, 2018. Mr. Lowry has requested that the property be rezoned to highway business. This will bring the property into our town ordinances. Scotty Harris made a motion to recommend in favor of the zoning map amendment, and therefore amend the Harmony Land Use Plan to include this parcel with a commercial designation, and making a finding that the approval is consistent with the newly amended future land use map designation and that said approval is reasonable and in the public interest and furthers the goals of the Future Land Use Plan because it conforms with the Land Use Map, adjacent property is commercial, it is situated suitably for commercial use, and traffic impacts will not exceed capacity. Julia Clanton seconded the motion. Motion carried with a vote of 4 in favor and 0 against. Adjournment Julia Clanton made a motion to adjourn the meeting. John Ray Campbell seconded the motion. Motion carried. Town Clerk___________________________________Mayor____________________________

title: Board of Aldermen Meeting - December 7, 2020
text: TOWN OF HARMONY MEETING MINUTES Town of Harmony 3389 Harmony Hwy, Harmony, NC 28634 704-546-2339 DATE: December 7, 2020 TIME: 4:00 PM ATTENDEES: Lee Matney, Mayor N Sankey Gaither - Council Member Julia Clanton - Council Member Doug Galliher – Council Member Scotty Harris – Council Member AGENDA: Call to Order: Mayor Matney Invocation: Council Member Harris Pledge of Allegiance: Council Member Clanton Approval of minutes: Julia Clanton made a motion to approve the November 2nd minutes. Scotty Harris seconded the motion. Motion carried. Scotty made a motion to approve the November 23rd minutes. Buddy Gaither seconded the motion. Motion carried. Public Comment Period: Each speaker is asked to limit comments to 3 minutes. The total comment period will be 15 minutes or less. Citizens should sign up with the Town Clerk to speak to the board by 3:00 pm on the Thursday prior to the meeting on Monday night. At the time of sign-up speakers should state their subject or the matter of concern Speakers should be the Town Board is interested in hearing the concerns of the speakers, however speakers should not expect Board action or deliberation on the subject matter brought up during the Public Comment segment. Topics requiring further investigation will be referred to the appropriate town officials or staff and may be scheduled for a future agenda. Thank you for your consideration of the Town Council, staff and other speakers. Tony Brewer, an associate with Eddie Carrick CPA, who performed the audit for the town was welcomed to the meeting. He remined the group that the audit is a public document and is open to any citizen who wishes to see it. He told the group that the “Unassigned Fund Balance” is at 404% which is very good. If we operated at the rate we do now and did not collect any more money, we could sustain ourselves for 4 years. He told the group that the sewer collection rate was 98.5% which was above the state average. Julia asked if he saw any “red” flags for us? Tony said that Harmony has always been healthy financially and has always been conservative. He said that sewer is at a break even point and that due to the age of our system we need to prepare for expensive break downs. We may need to think about raising our rate to be better prepared for the break downs when they happen. Matthew Todd and Leslie Meadows from the Iredell County Zoning Board along with property owner Amanda Loftis of Eagle Mills Investments spoke to the group about rezoning 3/10 of an acre on Highland Pt. Ave. from residential to residential/office. The planning staff supports the rezoning. Julia made a motion to accept the zoning proposal. Buddy seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. OLD BUSINESS: “Welcome to Harmony” sign – Has been put up Mulch at playground area at park – no update The proposed amendment to the Town Ordinances (Article 4 – Section 2.76) Approval and Signing Contracts: Julia made a motion to adopt the ordinance. Scotty seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. Doug and Buddy took the guys from Envirolink to the WWTP and to pump stations # 2 and # 3 so they could give us a proposal and cost. They were very attentative on the tour and got a clear picture of what we are looking for. They thought we are in good shape. The question will be, can we afford them. W. Memorial Hwy Pump Station Roadway – Work is continuing on the road. NEW BUSINESS: Grose Street – Mickey Vestal residence – there is a hole approximately 12’ deep at the man hole. County Boy will look at it. They think it could be an old culvert. They don’t think it is a breach in the sewer line. The contract for snow removal for the town from Charles Trivette was presented to the board. He is not asking for an increase in cost for removing the snow. His terms and charges remain the same as in the previous contract. Julia asked if we have a back-up in place in the event Charles is unable to remove the snow. Lee will find someone to serve as back-up. Julia made a motion to accept Charles’ contract. Scotty seconded the motion. Motion closed 4-0. Town office will be closed December 24th and 25th for Christmas. Next board meeting will be January 4th, 2021. It was brought up that the Christmas tree at the intersection needs to be replaced. The town of Troutman has a nice one. It was suggested that we call Troutman and find out where they got theirs. ADJOURNMENT: As there was no other business, Julia made a motion to adjourn the meeting. Doug seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. ______________________________ ________________________ Town Clerk Mayor

He found out that the privacy fence at the park is on his property about 5’ for a length of about 60’. Chris said that he would like to extend the existing privacy fence past his garage. If the town would be willing to furnish the material and Doug and Tim would help him, he would be satisfied with this instead of having to move the fence. Julia said this was a reasonable request. Julia made a motion that the town furnish the materials and have Doug and Tim help Chris extend the privacy fence past Chris’ garage. Scotty seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. Doug told the council that the split rail fence at the park is in bad shape and town needs to consider replacing it. He also said that perhaps the community center board would be willing to use the money raised from the July 4th breakfast to help with the cost. Discussion followed about the type of fencing to use and the height of the new fence. Scotty suggested that some breaks be left in the fence for pass through. Mayor Matney will get some bids for the fencing. Waste Water Treatment – Steve Lambert has sent a request asking for a $5.00 increase in pay for himself, J D Powell, Scotty Harris and Anthony Gilbert. After discussion, Julia made a motion to table the letter until Steve meets with the board to discuss some issues that were brought up. Doug seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. ADJOURNMENT: Julia made a motion to adjourn. Doug seconded. Motion carried 4-0. ______________________________ ________________________ Town Clerk Mayor Called Meeting after the public meeting for the purpose of discussing a pay increase for the Town Clerk/Finance Director.
