title: Board of Aldermen Meeting - February 4, 2019
text: Town of Harmony Meeting Minutes Town of Harmony North Carolina 3389 Harmony Highway, Harmony, NC 28634 704-546-2339 DATE: February 4, 2019 TIME: 7:00 PM ATTENDEES: Lee Matney, Mayor John Ray Campbell – Alderman Julia Clanton – Alderman Doug Galliher – Alderman Scotty Harris - Alderman AGENDA: Call to Order: Mayor Matney Invocation: Alderman Harris Pledge of Allegiance: Alderman Clanton Approval of previous Months Minutes Julia Clanton made a motion to approve the minutes of the January 7th, meeting – Scotty Harris seconded the motion. Motion carried. Julia made a motion to approve the minutes of the special meeting on January 7th and January 15th, 2018. Doug Galliher seconded the motion. Motion carried. Public Comment Period: Notes on the Comment Period Each speaker is asked to limit comments to 3 minutes. The total comment period will be 15 minutes or less. Citizens should sign up with the Town Clerk to speak to the board by 3:00pm on the Thursday prior to the meeting on Monday night. At the time of sign-up, speakers should state their subject or the matter of concern. Speakers should be aware the Town Board is interested in hearing the concerns of the speakers; however speakers should not expect Board action or deliberation on the subject matter brought up during the Public Comment segment. Topics requiring further investigation will be referred to the appropriate town officials or staff and may be scheduled for a future agenda. Thank you for your consideration of the Town Council, staff, and other speakers. . Melissa Gaither from the Harmony Library thanked the group for the $500.00 donation. She asked that instead of writing a check for the full amount, she would ask for reimbursement as money is spent. She also spoke to the group regarding activities planned at the library. Old Business: Cemetery Clean-Up Ordinance – Notices were posted throughout Harmony and at the cemetery regarding the ordinance for clean-up dates at the cemetery. Going forward, a copy of the ordinance and rules and regulations will be given to each person who purchases a cemetery plot. Clean-up dates will also be shown on sewer bills at appropriate dates. Julia Clanton made a motion to pass the ordinance. Scotty Harris seconded. Motion carried (4-0). Cemetery Mowing – Tommy Frye has asked the Board for a $15.00 increase for each time he mows the cemetery. This would bring his bid up to $309.00 per mowing. Blake Renegar has also submitted a bid for the mowing the cemetery. His bid was for $275,00 per mowing. Tommy Thompson submitted a bid of $300.00 per mowing or $280.00 per mowing if we paid him for 12 months instead of just per mowing. After discussion, Julia Clanton made a motion that we accept the bid from Blake Renegar. John Ray Campbell seconded the motion. Motion carried (4-0) Mayor Matney and Wanda Edwards met on Monday, February 4th with CPA’s Brian Gantt and Joe Haney. We discussed what we are needing from a CPA at this time. Their suggestion is that since we have changed computer systems, they should check that all beginning balances were transferred to the new system correctly. We will get a cost for their services. “Welcome to Harmony” sign that was destroyed by a wreck will be replaced. Their insurance company has been contacted and they will issue a check to replace the sign and replace broken blocks plus labor. Scotty suggested that this would be a good time to move the sign to the new town limits due to the annexation of the Lowry property. New Business Sewer Ordinance – Discussion was brought up about proposed changes to the sewer ordinance. Those changes are: (1) Set deposit for new customers on sewer as: $75.00 for residences and $100.00 for businesses. (2) We will send a “Late Payment” letter to customers after 35 days (3) Reconnect fees will be set at $35.00 Julia made a motion to approve changes to the sewer ordinance. Scotty seconded the motion. Motion carried. (4-0) South State Bank – Council members were given a copy of a letter received by the Town stating that the South State Bank in Statesville would be closing at the end of May and will consolidate with the South State Bank in Mooresville. We have 2 CD’s at South State. We would like to move those CD’s to another bank to avoid having to go to Mooresville. Julia suggested moving them to Bank of America. Lee asked about moving them to First Bank in Harmony. Debbie Haynes, Branch Manager in Harmony, told Lee that she has the authority to match the interest rates of any other bank. After discussion, John Ray Campbell made a motion to cash in the CD that matures March 14, 2019 and bring that money to First Bank in Harmony. The other CD matures September 22, 2019. At that time, we will cash in that CD also and move the money to First Bank. Doug Galliher seconded the motion. Motion carried (4-0) Mayor Matney told the group that he is working with Sgt. Mike Benfield from the Iredell County Sheriff’s office to grant them permission to enforce the Town ordinances. Mayor Matney has been contacted by a car club out of Statesville that will be sponsoring a car show to benefit Hospice. They have asked the Town to sponsor the car show. Julia stated that as a governing body she is not sure this is something we should do. We are using tax payer money and this money should be used to maintain the town and not for donations. All agreed. Adjournment Julia made a motion to adjourn. John Ray seconded. Motion carried. Town Clerk___________________________________Mayor____________________________

title: Board of Aldermen Meeting - February 5, 2024
text: Town of Harmony 3389 Harmony Hwy, Harmony, NC 28634 704-546-2339 DATE: February 5, 2024 TIME: 4:00 PM ATTENDEES: Sean Turner, Mayor Chris Pierce - Council Member Scotty Harris - Council Member Jared Clark – Council Member Brandon Angell – Council Member Wanda Edwards – Town Clerk AGENDA: Call to Order: Mayor Turner Invocation: Council Member: Jared Clark Pledge of Allegiance: Approval of minutes: Jared Clark made a motion to approve the January 8th, 2024 minutes. Brandon Angell seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. Brandon made a motion to approve the January 25th, 2024 minutes. Scotty Harris seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. Public Comment Period: Each speaker is asked to limit comments to 3 minutes. The total comment period will be 15 minutes or less. Citizens should sign up with the Town Clerk to speak to the board by 3:00 pm on the Thursday prior to the meeting on Monday night. At the time of sign-up speakers should state their subject or the matter of concern Speakers should be the Town Board is interested in hearing the concerns of the speakers, however speakers should not expect Board action or deliberation on the subject matter brought up during the Public Comment segment. Topics requiring further investigation will be referred to the appropriate town officials or staff and may be scheduled for a future agenda. Thank you for your consideration of the Town Council, staff and other speakers. Lacy Blankenship requested that the council make an exception to the ordinance pertaining to farm animals being inside the city limits and grant her permission to keep two dairy goats on her family property located at 179 Little Wilkesboro Rd. She said they would eat overgrown vegetation and weeds on the property and contribute fertilizer for the garden. She also said they would be a good source of dairy and companionship. She said breeding season is once a year and the kids would be sold. She said they would be in a fenced area, but there was no guarantee of a mishap. Board advised they would take it under consideration and get back to her with a decision. OLD BUSINESS: CONTRACTS: Contract for Tommy’s Total Lawn Care, LLC is up for renewal. Tommy has not increased his price. All agreed that he does a good job. Scotty Harris made a motion to approve Tommy’s contract from 3/01/2024 – 2/28/2025. Jared Clark seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. PLAYGROUND MULCH – Bids were submitted by Renegar Property Maintenance and Tommy’s Total Lawn Care. After review and discussion of the bids, Jared made a motion to accept the bid from Tommy’s Total Lawn Care. Motion was seconded by Scotty Harris. Motion carried 4-0. HOUSE – Sheriff Campbell will set a time to come and look at the house. Mayor Turner announced plans are being made for a Community Wide Easter Egg Hunt / Celebration , a Fourth of July parade and a Corn-Hole tournament and Chili Cook-off. FARMER’S MARKET – Nancy Keith and Melinda Roberts who are County Extension agents spoke to the council about starting a farmer’s market and a 4-H club. They said the Iredell Co. Extension was willing to help with rules, regulations and safety of a farmer’s market. They have specialists who help start farmer’s markets. All products must be farmer produced. Produce cannot be bought and brought in to sell. Must have legal for trade scales that must be calibrated. Melinda said they are looking for a 4-H leader in North Iredell. Melinda runs the Master Gardener Program and hopes to have one at the farmer’s market. The extension will advertise for all farmer’s products. We need to identify a manager and a location for the market and safety of the location should be a consideration. Cemetery Fence – put on “hold” Theatre Property – Mayor Turner has talked with contractor to come look at building and give an idea of work to be done. He has also been looking for grants to revitalize old buildings. Mayor told the board that we have Jeff McNeely, Vickie Sawyer, Gray Mills, and Mitchell Setzer working for Iredell County. INTERSECTION - Vickie told the Mayor to get a plan for the intersection of Hwy 21 and Hwy 901. Jeff said that even after DOT did not consider enough of a hazard for a red light, we can push it farther, but it may take money from Harmony. He said a round-a-bout is safer. He also told the group that the Governor has funds that we may be able to get due to safety reasons. He feels like there is a need for it. He said he would hate to see a round-a-bout there due to the large trucks that travel through the intersection. He said the round-a-bout would have to be so large it would take up a lot of the area at the town square. Brandon asked is there a way to see a list of any available funding. Mr. McNeely said “not really.” He said to think about what we need; prioritize our needs and he will work towards it. Our surplus dollars in the state are getting smaller. They are cutting taxes. Less tax dollars coming in = less surplus. JEFF JONES – Talked about the kick-off meeting with McGill Associates. Brought up that a 4” check valve that stops back flowing needs to be repaired. Lead time probably two weeks. Chub Gunner will set up an access point at Little Wilkesboro pump station in preparation for by-pass. Presented and explained a print-out he had prepared explaining a summary of the remaining $104,000.00 ARP money and the quotes he has received for work to be done utilizing this money. Telemetry system to be purchased – after discussing the pros and cons between the Mission System and Dorsett, Jared made a motion to purchase the Mission telemetry system. Brandon seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. Jeff also presented a quote from Associated Metal Works, Inc. to furnish labor and equipment to fabricate and replace effluent box at the WWTP. Scotty made a motion to move forward with replacing the box. Chris Pierce seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. Jeff will get a quote from Associated Metal Works to replace rail and a quote to repair gate. Jeff said he will update the form as he gets new information and have it available for all to see. Jared asked about noise from blowers. Jeff said when we are able to purchase encapsulated blowers and add VFDs they would be quitter. Jared would like to get quieter blowers as soon as we can. Hayes Street - Question was asked “Do we want to put a stop to allowing doublewide mobile homes to be brought in?” This would be something for our Planning Board to decide. PLANNING BOARD – Mayor Turner introduced members of our newly formed Planning Board – Martin Reavis (not present), Forest Breedlove (not present), Dereck Holbrook, Doug Galliher and Chris Harris. Mayor Turner will meet with board this month along with Matthew Todd. Question was asked “do we need two alternates?” Board said “no need.” Planning Board will meet quarterly. They will update the Land Use Plan from 2017. EQUIPMENT – Jeff will contact Nixon to service generator. Doug will get UTV service. Jeff will use UTV on sewer line outfalls as Mayor wants it used more often. DUMPSTER – Lowry’s is using 2 trash cans – would like town to furnish small dumpster. Do we want to provide it for others? Town does not pay for dumpsters being emptied. Due to costs and having to provide for others, council decided to stand back from it. Meeting was adjourned for Personnel Matter Meeting Back in Session Question – why have Christmas decorations not been taken down? Brandon and Jared will get pricing for a projector with sound for the Town Hall – After approval from board, they will purchase and install. Lacy Blankenship – Jared thinks it is a core liberty to be able to provide your own food. If farm animals are to be allowed, there will have to be permitting and inspections. Mayor Turner said we will have to adjust the ordinances. There should be restrictions. Chris said they should have to talk with their neighbors. Jared said they should only have to notify the neighbors. Matter was tabled for a special meeting on February 13th @ 6 p.m. COMMUNITY CENTER – They will be having the Fourth of July breakfast. We need to get a list of what needs to be updated at the building. It may be that the town wants to partner up with them. The new president is Laura Elliott. Chris wants to see a legal document between the Community Center Board and the Town. Brandon says we need additional parking and bathrooms at the park. ADJOURNMENT: As there was no other business: Scotty made a motion to adjourn. Brandon seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. ______________________________ ________________________ Town Clerk Mayor

text: TOWN OF HARMONY MEETING MINUTES Town of Harmony 3389 Harmony Hwy, Harmony, NC 28634 704-546-2339 DATE: January 6, 2020 TIME: 7:00 PM ATTENDEES: Lee Matney, Mayor N. Sankey Gaither - Council Member Julia Clanton - Council Member Doug Galliher – Council Member Scotty Harris – Council Member AGENDA: Call to Order: Mayor Matney Invocation: Council Member Harris Pledge of Allegiance: Council Member Clanton Approval of previous month’s minutes: Julia Clanton made a motion to approve the December 9th, 2019 old minutes. Scotty seconded the motion. Motion carried 3-0. Scotty made a motion to approve the December 9th, 2019 new minutes. Doug seconded the motion. Motion carried 3-0. Topics requiring further investigation will be referred to the appropriate town officials or staff and may be scheduled for a future agenda. Thank you for your consideration of the Town Council, staff and other speakers. Melissa Gaither from the Harmony Library told the group about planned activities for the winter at the library. Mayor Matney asked if she had voter registration cards at the library and she does. Tony Brewer, from Eddie Carrick CPA, who performed the 2018-2019 audit spoke to the council about the audit. He said the town received a clean opinion based on the audit. He said the audit is a public document and can be examined by anyone who wishes to see it. In the General Fund the miscellaneous line is down from 2018 due to the sale of some assets in 2018. The expenses are down for 2019 due to some street repairs and paving the parking lot that was done in 2018. The Unassigned Fund Balance is 452% and that is good. He stated that if we did not collect any more money and continued spending at the same rate, we would be able to operate for 4.5 years. The sewer collection rate is 98.49% which is above the state average. The revenue is greater than the expense. He advised us to be diligent about keeping a close eye on the sewer revenue and expenses to be sure that we do not get in a financial hardship. At some point, it may be necessary to raise the sewer rates. He thanked Mayor and clerk for having all reports and information necessary for the audit readily available to him. OLD BUSINESS: Julia asked about the ordinance violation letters that were to be sent out by Ms. Dixon. She has been in the process of setting up her new office. She hopes to begin sending out the letters this week. Julia asked if someone could speak to the Harmony Fire Department and let them know that the gutter at the back where they do the cooking is falling down and ask them to fasten the gutter back up to the building. Julia also asked about the information sign the town has – what were we going to do about it. Tim and Doug are going to clean the sign to improve the appearance. NEW BUSINESS: Julia also noted that some of the headstones at the cemetery are getting really dirty. She asked if we could hire someone to come out and pressure wash the headstones. Doug noted that we would have to be really careful, that pressure washing could damage some of the old headstones. Julia asked if we could call Statesville Marble & Granite and ask them how to clean the headstones without causing damage. A few of the headstones are broken. Can we get a cost to repair them? Scotty asked if anyone knew why paving of Hwy 21 was stopped at the city limits. No one knew what the plan was. Doug talked about Matthew 25. He said they were only open 7 hours a week now. He wondered if we could have the director come to a meeting and give an update. Mayor Matney told the group that Dale Hague had asked about the VFW and DAV using the white house that we use for storage for a meeting once a month. Doug said the house needed a lot of work done to it. There is no heat or air conditioning in the house. Julia suggested them using the community center and charge only the cost of Tim cleaning – other suggestion was that maybe they could use the old fire department. ADJOURNMENT: Julia made a motion to adjourn the meeting. Scotty seconded the motion. Motion carried 3-0. ______________________________ ________________________ Town Clerk Mayor

title: Board of Aldermen Meeting - January 7, 2019
text: Town of Harmony Meeting Minutes Town of Harmony North Carolina 3389 Harmony Highway, Harmony, NC 28634 704-546-2339 DATE: January 7, 2019 TIME: 7:00 PM ATTENDEES: Lee Matney, Mayor John Ray Campbell – Alderman Julia Clanton – Alderman Doug Galliher – Alderman Scotty Harris - Alderman AGENDA: Call to Order: Mayor Matney Invocation: Alderman Campbell Pledge of Allegiance: Alderman Clanton Approval of previous Months Minutes Julia Clanton made a motion to approve the minutes of the December 3rd meeting – Scotty Harris seconded the motion. Motion carried. Julia made a motion to approve the minutes of the special meeting on December 12th, 2018. John Ray Campbell seconded the motion. Motion carried. Public Comment Period: Notes on the Comment Period Each speaker is asked to limit comments to 3 minutes. The total comment period will be 15 minutes or less. Citizens should sign up with the Town Clerk to speak to the board by 3:00pm on the Thursday prior to the meeting on Monday night. At the time of sign-up, speakers should state their subject or the matter of concern. Speakers should be aware the Town Board is interested in hearing the concerns of the speakers; however speakers should not expect Board action or deliberation on the subject matter brought up during the Public Comment segment. Topics requiring further investigation will be referred to the appropriate town officials or staff and may be scheduled for a future agenda. Thank you for your consideration of the Town Council, staff, and other speakers. . Melissa Gaither from the Harmony Library spoke to the group regarding activities planned at the library. They will have the Star Lab which is a blow up planetarium owned by the State Library during the first week in March. Possible sites for the planetarium to be placed are the Life Center at the Baptist Church, the fire department and possibly the Harmony School gym. Melissa also shared with the group other activities planned at the library. Tony Brewer with Eddie Carrick, CPA was present to review and share findings with the council concerning the recent audit. He thanked the council for allowing their firm to conduct the audit and told them they want to be an asset for the town. Each council member was given a copy of the audit and Tony explained where the town is, where it has been and where he feels it is going. He explained that revenue was down $50,000., but this was due to a storm water reimbursement that the town had received the previous year and did not receive in this audit period. Expenses were up for this audit period, but he explained that this was due to the loan for Matthew 25, the purchase of the land and the expenses of building the parking lot and additional street repairs. Sewer revenue was up and expenses were also up, but he felt the additional expense was due to maintenance and repairs. He talked about the Unassigned Fund Balance and said this was a guideline showing that if we spent at the same rate as in 2017-2018 with no income received, we could stay open for 2.5 years. He also told the council that the town’s tax collection rate is 98.25% which is above the state average. He said water/sewer looks good for 2018 – 2019. Old Business: Julia reminded the group that at the last meeting, the library had asked for a donation to assist with their programs – Julia made a motion to give the library a $500.00 donation. Doug Galliher seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. Manhole cover on Grose Street has been repaired. Shane Reynolds from Iredell County brought a frame up and Tim Trivette and Doug repaired it. “Jake Brake” signs have been put up by the DOT. Mowing Contract –Tommy Thompson submitted a bid for the mowing, for mowing the cemetery (that has been done by Tommy Frye mowing), and for the fertilizing, aerating, etc. (that was previously done by Blakely Landscape Service). He submitted bids for each of the areas and his bids for the cemetery and lawn service show the cost for each time service is performed and the cost if we contract to pay him for 12 months. Scotty question that he showed trimming the shrubs 1 time a year and asked if he would trim another time each year at no additional cost. Doug also wants him to trim around the signs. Scotty told the group that a decision regarding the fertilizing, etc. at the park needs to be made soon because this work will need to be done next month. Julia made a motion to accept Tommy’s bid for mowing and for the work at the park. Scotty seconded. Motion carried 4-0. As for the cemetery, Mayor will talk with Tommy Frye to see if he wants to continue mowing the cemetery and bring this information back to the council. Mayor will also get a bid from Mr. Renegar if Tommy does not want to mow the cemetery. Town Clerk asked if there was anyone interested in having direct deposit for their check – no one wanted it. New Business Council was given a copy of a new proposed ordinance concerning clean up days at the cemetery. We need to do a public notice before the ordinance can be adopted. Notices will be posted 10 days prior to the next town meeting. Ordinance can be adopted at that time. Discussion was also brought up about a sign between Harmony Galaxy Food Center and Barkers store causing a hazard as drivers are pulling out onto Hwy 21 and sign is blocking their view of oncoming traffic. Lee will check with DOT to see if sign needs to be moved. Adjournment Julia made a motion to adjourn. John Ray seconded. Motion carried. Town Clerk___________________________________Mayor____________________________

title: Board of Aldermen Meeting - January 8, 2024
text: Town of Harmony 3389 Harmony Hwy, Harmony, NC 28634 704-546-2339 DATE: January 8, 2024 TIME: 4:00 PM ATTENDEES: Sean Turner, Mayor Chris Pierce - Council Member Scotty Harris - Council Member Jared Clark – Council Member Brandon Angell – Council Member Wanda Edwards – Town Clerk AGENDA: Call to Order: Mayor Turner Invocation: Council Member Pierce Pledge of Allegiance: Approval of minutes: Scotty Harris made a motion to approve the December 4th, 2023 minutes with the correction of adding his name to those sworn in by Jim Mixon. Brandon Angell seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. Scotty made a motion to approve the December 14th, 2023 minutes with the correction that count to adjourn the meeting be corrected to read 4-0 (printed as 47-0). Brandon Angell seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. Public Comment Period: Each speaker is asked to limit comments to 3 minutes. The total comment period will be 15 minutes or less. Citizens should sign up with the Town Clerk to speak to the board by 3:00 pm on the Thursday prior to the meeting on Monday night. At the time of sign-up speakers should state their subject or the matter of concern Speakers should be the Town Board is interested in hearing the concerns of the speakers, however speakers should not expect Board action or deliberation on the subject matter brought up during the Public Comment segment. Topics requiring further investigation will be referred to the appropriate town officials or staff and may be scheduled for a future agenda. Thank you for your consideration of the Town Council, staff and other speakers. Mayor Turner and award sponsors presented the awards to those who won in the different categories for the Christmas Parade. Mayor Turner also recognized and thanked members of the Harmony Fire Dept. who hung the Christmas decorations for the town. Melissa Gaither from the Harmony Library told the group about activities planned at the library during the month of January. She said that on the 27th of January they will have a program detailing beneficial uses for native plants. On February 8th they will have the Family Book Club and the Discovery Club will meet on Tuesdays at 4 p.m. On February 21st at 1:00 p.m. Bright Star Theatre will present “African Folk Tales.” OLD BUSINESS: House: Mayor Turner hasn’t had an opportunity to talk with Sheriff Campbell about the possibility of the ICSO using the house as an office. We need to see what the cost would be to install WIFI. Mayor will get Sheriff Campbell and Bill Hamby to come out and see if it might fit their needs and what can be worked out. Planning Board – We need to move forward with establishing a Planning Board and we need 5 people to serve on the board. Those suggested to serve on the board: Chris Harris, Forest Breedlove, Dereck Holbrook, Martin Reavis and Doug Galliher. Mayor will reach out to these to see if they will be willing to serve. Questions to be decided are (1) how often will they meet – (July 10th 2023 Council voted and passed to have Planning Board meet quarterly) (2) Pay – Scotty told the group that the amount of pay had been decided on and voted on in previous meeting. (July 10th, 2023 Council voted and passed to pay board members $75.00 for quarterly meeting and $50.00 for any extra meeting.) Matthew Todd and Christy Madison are willing to help set up the board. Mayor said a requirement should be that they have to live inside the city limits. Bids for snow removal, Town and WWTP mowing – Mayor Turner told the group that he stopped the bidding process for mowing due to Tommy’s Total Lawn Care not increasing the cost of mowing for 2024 and he is doing a great job. He stated that he did not think it fair to put it out for bid. For this bid we would want to be sure that the bidder had the same number of people working as Tommy so the job could be done in one day. Mayor Turner told the group that we received bids from Charles Trivette for snow removal ($2,800.00) and Renegar Property Maintenance ($2,500.00). Chris Pierce made a motion to accept the bid from Renegar Property Maintenance for snow removal. Scotty Harris seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. This fall we will need to get bids for leaf removal and make the contract detailed of what is expected.H Meeting Time – After discussion, Brandon made a motion that we change the time for the Town Board meeting from 4:00 p.m. to 6:00 p.m. Chris seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. From Clerk: Reminded Mayor and new council members that they are required to take the “Ethics Training Class.” Love Valley has asked if we would like to meet with them and take it together. Cost for a teacher would be $500.00 for Harmony and Love Valley each. They decided they would rather take the class on their own and town would reimburse them the cost of the class. Grant Gaither is working on updating our Web Site. Updated council on work that is performed by Doug Galliher and Tim Trivette – handle 811s, they know all about the cemetery and clean old flowers, etc. off as needed, tend to the flags at the cemetery and park, check the community center after each use, clean the community center monthly, clean the town hall, keep trash emptied at the park, help when park shelter is rented out and many more jobs. NEW BUSINESS: We need to appoint a delegate and alternate to Centralina Council of Government – Jared agreed to be the delegate and Brandon will be the alternate. Priscilla Holmes was asked to serve as a delegate to the Iredell County Parks and Recreation Board. Field beside Community Bldg – Since we are not leasing out this field anymore, Mayor suggested that we see if Gene Powers will sow grass there and we will get Tommy to keep it bush hogged. We will get a price from Tommy to bush hog it or may see if this is something Tim and Doug can do. There is a place close to the porta-jon that we can utilize for additional parking. Sewer Taps/Manhole Covers – We are working to be sure only one structure is hooked to a tap. If someone outside the city limits wants to hook to our sewer system they will need to self-annex into the town. Over the next six months Mayor Turner wants to go over town properties to be sure that those connected to sewer are being billed and those who should be paying the assessment fee are being billed also. Jeff Jones – Jared Wright from McGill Associates would like to do a kick-off meeting for the Inventory/Assessment Grant. They will be able to help us set in-town and out-of-town rates, give us a priority list of Capital Improvements and help us plan for the future of our sewer system. Jeff would like for the Mayor and Council to set a date and time for the kick-off. McGill will come to any board meeting to answer questions or be of any assistance. Telemetry Upgrade – Jeff said that he would be working on the by-pass at Linda Drive and then the telemetry. Rain water is getting into the system – does not need to. Telemetry is very out dated. Scope of work for the new grant is going to be sewer based unless we tell them different, but we have to let them know. Jeff said we need to replace the box at the plant ASAP. Mayor Turner told Jeff to get a quote from Associated Metals to make the box. Jeff said we have to find someone to put it in and it has to be done quickly. Quotes for telemetry upgrade: Lord & Company - $110,386.00 / Mission - $33,562.41 (cellular) and Dorsett - $37,452.00 (radio). Mayor Turner wants a check list of what Jeff is doing. Jeff said he will provide daily journal which shows jobs performed each day. Jeff asked how often the board wants him to come to the meetings. Harmony Café Building – Mayor Turner said we need a restaurant in Harmony. This building is for sale. Eddie Gaither, who owns the building, asked for the town to purchase the building. Chris said the building will have to be torn down. The old theater building has roof problems. Price asked for the property is for prime bare land. Eddie previously reached out to Representative McNeely about securing a grant to repair the roof. He was told he could not get the grant, only the town could. Mayor Turner does not know if there is money to re-do historical property. Money not available for café building. The Napa store is connected to the old theater part of the building and NAPA owns that part of the building. Mayor Turner says a restaurant will help out businesses in town. He knows a couple of developers who might be interested. All agreed that for the best interest of the town, the price is not a good buy. Mayor Turner is going to reach back out to Eddie and to tell him we are going to have to sit back on $450,000.00. Local business owners in our town may invest in our town. Intersection – Mayor Turner has spoken with Vickie Sawyer about what might be done at the intersection of Hwy 21 and Hwy 901. Mrs. Sawyer said to get a plan of what we want and get back to her. We have to work to build our town up. Chris said that 97% of the people he had spoken with were in favor of a round-about. Farmers Market – Mayor Turner will be working to bring a Farmers Market back to Harmony. He will be in Raleigh in February meeting with Comm. Trexler. John Gallina – urged us to reach out to Iredell Economic Development for help. Park Playground – We need to put mulch around the playground equipment. We will bring quotes to the February meeting. Need to think about hiring a company to inspect playground equipment for safety. We will be reviewing alternatives for weekly trash collection for 279 homes. Mayor Turner is reaching out to other Mayors in county re partnering with different people and agencies to be able to get a better direction of where to go for help. Evergreen Heating & Air – has decided not to move forward with purchasing the old A&H Stained Glass building. There is no easement off of Highland Pt. Ave to get to the back of the building. Owner of the building, N. Sankey Gaither, will not sell an easement. Evergreen does not want to lease an easement. They will be looking for other property in Harmony. ADJOURNMENT: As there was no other business: Jared made a motion to adjourn. Brandon seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. ______________________________ ________________________ Town Clerk Mayor

title: Board of Aldermen Meeting - July 1, 2024
text: Town of Harmony 3389 Harmony Hwy, Harmony, NC 28634 704-546-2339 DATE: July 1, 2024 TIME: 4:00 PM ATTENDEES: Sean Turner, Mayor Chris Pierce - Council Member Scotty Harris - Council Member Jared Clark – Council Member Brandon Angell – Council Member Wanda Edwards – Town Clerk AGENDA: Call to Order: Mayor Turner Invocation: Mayor Sean Turner Pledge of Allegiance: Jared Clark joined the meeting by video. Approval of minutes: Brandon Angell made a motion to approve the June 3rd , 2024 minutes. Chris Pierce seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. Brandon made a motion to approve the June 12th minutes. Scotty Harris seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. Public Comment Period: Each speaker is asked to limit comments to 3 minutes. The total comment period will be 15 minutes or less. Citizens should sign up with the Town Clerk to speak to the board by 3:00 pm on the Thursday prior to the meeting on Monday night. At the time of sign-up speakers should state their subject or the matter of concern Speakers should be the Town Board is interested in hearing the concerns of the speakers, however speakers should not expect Board action or deliberation on the subject matter brought up during the Public Comment segment. Topics requiring further investigation will be referred to the appropriate town officials or staff and may be scheduled for a future agenda. Thank you for your consideration of the Town Council, staff, and other speakers. Melissa Gaither from the Harmony Library told the group about the summer reading program Kick-Off which was held on June 4th with a good attendance. On June 17th from 2 PM – 3 PM Allison Woods presented a program on “Owl Pellets” which was also a success. Detective Ernest McNeeley introduced two of the teenagers who had broken into and vandalized the white house the town owns behind the office. They apologized for the damage they caused. They will also pay for and make all repairs to the house. Matthew Rogers, who ran through our fence and fled the scene also came in and apologized and will make restitution for the damages. OLD BUSINESS: FLAG DAY: Discussion was held on the success of Flag Day. Mayor suggested that we should make a donation to help pay for the food that was served. Brandon made a motion that we donate $150.00 towards the cost of the food. Jared seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. COMMUNITY CENTER BATHROOMS: We have received no other quote other than Cory Pennell’s for $4800.00. Mayor Turner suggested that we wait until after the July 4th Breakfast to discuss with Community Center Board. PLANNING BOARD: Board will meet quarterly unless something comes up that requires an additional meeting. Pay will be the same as County pays their Planning Board. CAMERAS AT WWTP: Will be installed by the end of July. PRESSURE WASHING: Tim Souther did a good job. TWO MEETINGS PER MONTH; Jared said we should try to do a 45 minute meeting. Brandon asked what is the difference between a second meeting and a special meeting? Brandon suggested we could call a special meeting if needed and if not needed don’t. Mayor said leave it as special meeting. Tabled until the August meeting. WEB SITE: The color scheme has been changed to royal blue. We want the Town Seal on the web site. Mayor had talked with Kadre Campbell about managing our social media. Jared said that we need to figure out what we want this person to do. We need board to come up with a list of what we want this person to do and e-mail it to clerk. Clerk will send it out to Mayor and council for review before the August meeting. Jared wants to see more reference to farming on our web site. NEW BUSINESS: McGILL ENGINEERING: Mayor Turner asked “Do we want to move away from McGill?” Jeff replied that Russell Byrd who is working with us now is as different as night and day from Jared. He is working on finding the GIS file. We gave them this file so they would not have to do the work. Jared saw the GIS and said he needed to figure out how to save us some money. Mayor has spoken with Slade who at one time worked for Wooten & Assoc., but has since gone out on his own. Mayor suggested that we give McGill one more month and if things aren’t better we’ll move on. LOVE’S STATION: Presented a copy of pricing to run force main line from sewer plant to Tomlin Mill exit. Estimate from West Consultants is $2,975,000.00. We need to know the amount of flow per day expected. Mayor said that he needs to talk with Beth Mull to apply for Golden Leaf for funding. Love’s has sent preliminary drawings to county. Sewer needs to be in by October, 2025. Jeff said they will have to do an Impact Study. If we do reclaimed water it will help with securing grant money. West Consultants did not quote for line for reclaimed water. Mayor told council that sometime at the first of August there will be a Legislative Event at Ralph Renegar’s. He told council they need to attend and talk with those in attendance and let them know what we are trying to do. LIFT STATION HWY 901 W: Jeff has talked with Jared Reed with Clearwater. They will be here Monday at 9:00 A.M. to pick up pump for repair. Discussed if we need to check dates on pumps to see when they were installed. This is the purpose of the AIA Grant. They will check date on each pump, etc. for estimated longevity. BLOWER MOTOR: 3 blowers are running. Cost of new motor is $600.00. They are in stock in Charlotte. Instead of purchasing a stand-by and letting it sit on a shelf until we need it (at which time it may sit there until the warranty expires), we will purchase one as needed. FARMERS MARKET: Has been moved to field behind Community Center. Mayor says Farmers Market eventually needs to be regional. VOLLYBALL NET: The net at the park needs to be replaced. Also, playground equipment needs to be inspected. Scotty will get a name and bring it back to us. STAGE: Clerk asked if we were still interested in purchasing a stage. Harmony Hill Camp Meeting would like to donate $500.00 towards the purchase. Scotty made a motion that we purchase the stage. Brandon seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. FALL FESTIVAL: Asked council to bring ideas to the next meeting. We need a committee to plan and carry out the event. ADJOURNMENT: As there was no other business: Brandon made a motion to adjourn. Scotty seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. ______________________________ ________________________ Town Clerk Mayor

text: Town of Harmony 3389 Harmony Hwy, Harmony, NC 28634 704-546-2339 DATE: July 11, 2022 TIME: 4:00 PM ATTENDEES: Lee Matney, Mayor N Sankey Gaither - Council Member Julia Clanton - Council Member Doug Galliher – Council Member Scotty Harris – Council Member AGENDA: Call to Order: Mayor Matney Invocation: Council Member Harris Pledge of Allegiance: Council Member Clanton Approval of minutes: Julia Clanton made a motion to approve the June 6th minutes. Thank you for your consideration of the Town Council, staff and other speakers. Mayor Matney welcomed the guests. Alex Grant from Winthrop Church was present to talk to the council about the Columbarium they purchased at Winthrop in 2019. He said there were 3 things to consider: # 1 - Size – determined by the number of niches you want # 2 – Do you want it U.S. made or imported? Very little difference in price # 3 - Quality – Big difference in quality. Some have gaps between niches. Winthrop chose to Purchase theirs from Georgia. It has 48 niches. 4 niches high x 6 wide. Base is 4’ x 8’. It Took up a little over 2 cemetery spaces. They chose bronze rosettes to put names on the Niches. Doors seal very tight. Columbarium is set on a flat pad. They limit the number of Lines to put on each door. Winthrop used a company from Yadkinville. Winecoff in Statesville can get the Columbarium also. In 2019 Winthrop paid $14,000., they charge $1,000. Per space. Derrick from Sir Speedy in Statesville spoke to the Council about replacing the sign that we have. He brought pictures of designs that they could provide for the town. No decision was made regarding replacing the sign. Mayor Matney closed the meeting for public comment. OLD BUSINESS: Lawson Property – Ms. Dixon is sending them a letter asking them to have their property mowed. No update on the Economic Development Grant. Sidewalk – Lee met with Justin Woolledge from Custom Concrete Development and walked all of the sidewalks to determine what repairs need to be made. Justin will do repairs but they do not do landscaping. Blake Renegar has agreed to repair any problems with landscaping. Justin will be able to do the work sometime around the middle of August. The total of his bid is $12,768.00 Scotty made a motion to go with Custom Concrete Development. Doug seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. Roof – Council reviewed the proposal from Dry-Tech Commercial Roofing to re-roof the front part of the Town Hall. The total of the bid is $24,137.00. Julia made a motion to have Dry-Tech re-roof the building. Scotty seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. Upstairs – Question was brought up – could we remove a window upstairs and replace it with a door. When we need to have work done on the camera that faces the bank, it is a struggle for the repairman to have to climb through the window to get onto the roof. Council agreed to have someone look at it and see how much it would cost to put a door in. WWTP Fence Line – Scotty asked “Who is the fence line on?” Buddy has talked with the lady there who said that Ray Lewis had mowed 20’ down the fence line and she would like to have it mowed. Doug said there is a dead tree that is going to fall on the fence. Vegetation is overgrown. Was suggested that maybe we could get Charles Trivette to go look at it and then Tommy can keep it up. Thank you for your consideration of the Town Council, staff and other speakers. Melissa Gaither from the Harmony Library was unable to attend the meeting. She sent brochures detailing activities planned at the library for the month which were shared with the group. Shawn Turner spoke to the council. He is building a new house on Woodland Bend and would like to connect to the town sewer line. The closest hook up point would be behind the Community Building. Shawn wants to pay to have a line installed from his home to be connected at the community center. He will have to install a grinder pump as there is a gradual up hill to the hook up at the community center. Shawn also stated that he would own this line and no one else would be allowed to connect to the line. After much discussion, Shawn was told that he would have to have an engineer come out and evaluate installing this line and get back to the council and a decision would be made after we hear from the engineer. Mayor Matney told Shawn that he has spoken with 2 engineers. After much discussion, Shawn was told that he could not use a 2” pipe, he will have to use standard size pipe, he will have to use an engineer and the line will belong to the town. Shawn asked if the town would pay for part of the cost of the engineer and part of the cost of having the line installed. He was told “no”. He would be responsible for all of the cost. The line would have to be designed by an engineer approved by the town. OLD BUSINESS: Council was told that letters for the properties belonging to Dorothy Moore, Remi Lavoi, Sue Lawson, and James Partin were sent out with the exception of Dorothy Moore. Mrs. Moore has just recently passed away, so out of respect she had not yet sent the letter. Board asked her to go ahead and send the letter to Luther Moore who will handle her estate. Cole Cass is hoping to install the cameras at the WWTP the week of July 19 – 25th. Town Clerk ,Wanda Edwards presented to the board budget amendments that needed to be approved. After reviewing the amendments, Scotty made a motion to approve the 2020-2021 budget amendments. Julia seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. Fence along school road – no one claims ownership to the fence. Harmony School says the fence does not belong to the school Privacy Fence on Pierce Property on Woodland Bend - Mr. Pierce is upset because we have not been out there to extend the fence so he wants it removed. Julia wants to have all town properties surveyed. We need to have park surveyed and put down permanent markers. Ask to get corners marked and this will be cheaper than a total survey. It was suggested that we remove fence from Pierce property and put up a chain link fence along the walking trail. Add for ORC - Council ask clerk to post ad for ORC in newspapers and other outlets. She also told the council that there is a lot of traffic in and out of this residence. Town will send a letter to this property owner regarding cleaning up the property. Deputies will be notified about the traffic going into this residence. She has a lot of unclaimed cats around her property. She has contacted animal control and they are not doing anything. She said that trucks with trailers were coming down Hayes St. and turning around in her driveway. She asked if the Town could put a “No Turn Around” sign at her driveway or was this something she would have to do. She was told that she would have to take care of putting up this sign. She spoke about the burned out trailer on Hayes St. and asked if the town could do anything about getting it cleaned up. She was told that the council does not know who owns this property, but would look at the ordinances and see what can be done. Melissa Gaither from the Harmony Library told the group about the summer programs the library has to offer. The summer reading program kicks off on June 15th at the Troutman Park. Bill Czerkie told the group that Duke Energy seems to be slacking off on trimming along the power lines. He asked if the Mayor would call Duke and see if they would trim some of the problem areas. Old Business: Bunch Johnson and Nicholson Funeral Homes strongly urged a meeting between the Town and Billy Jones, who previously dug the graves in the Harmony Cemetery. After the meeting, Mr. Jones agreed to resume digging the grave spots in the cemetery. Julia made a motion rescind the previous motion made at the May 6th meeting regarding hiring Drew Williard to dig the graves. Scotty seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. We have received bids from Country Boy Landscaping and Jem’s Grading and Paving to do the speed bumps on John Deere Drive. Bid prices were less if they were installed in conjunction with paving Grose Street. Julia said she had looked at the condition of Grose Street and Hayes St. She said that Grose Street was in worse condition at present time. Doug agreed with Julia. After discussion, Scotty made a motion to pave Grose Street and put in the speed bumps on John Deere Dr. Doug seconded. Motion carried 4-0. Mayor told council members that the “Speed Bump” signs are here at the office. Doug Galliher made a motion to appropriate money from one of our money markets to fund this project. Scotty seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. Mayor Matney told the Council that all the paperwork has been signed and returned to Michael Buchanan at NCDOT regarding lowering the speed limit inside the Town limits to 35 mph Town Clerk gave the Council a financial report showing the budget, where we are now and projecting where we anticipate being at the end of June. Council will meet on Monday, June 24th at 3 p.m. to approve the 2019-2020 budget. Town Clerk told the Board that Joe Haney from Gantt Malzi had spent the day in our office on May 23rd and he thought we were in good shape. New Business Mayor told the Council that he wants to work on an amendment to our ordinances regarding untagged/junked cars. We will have 2 open meetings prior to amending the ordinance. Mayor told the group that he has asked Town Attorney Rusty Chapman to modify the letter that we send out regarding ordinance violations to make it a stronger letter. Mayor has talked with Sheriff Campbell about enforcing the town ordinances. The Sheriff told the Mayor the ICSO does not have an Enforcement Officer. PUBLIC HEARING: Matthew Todd and Leslie Meadows were present to present a rezoning request from Joseph Blankenship for two properties he owns on Polly Anne Dr. (1.10 acres). At present it is zoned R20 for single family residences and he would like to change the zoning to Residential Office (RO). RO zoning would allow for multi-family residences. Since it was R20 water and sewer are already available. The audience was told that rezoning was only a first step and the only purpose of this meeting was for rezoning. Randy Harris spoke against the rezoning because he said “ it was gonna bring in junk, he don’t want a bunch of kids playing around and in his pasture – don’t want it – afraid of stealing and junk coming in.” Joseph Blankenship, owner of the property, said his plan is to build apartments for people 55 or older. Depending on the way his land lays out, he will only have between 10 – 14 apartments. Zoning wise there will be no outbuilding and no working on vehicles on the property. It will be a nice place for older people. He is planning on a U shaped building based on what will fit in the space. Not over 14 units under one roof. They will have sound barriers. If the rezoning is not approved, he could put in a couple of homes without rezoning. He was asked if there would be any restrictions as to the number of people living in the apartment. Answer – “Yes, that would be spelled out in the lease. Harris asked, “What is this going to do to his property?” Answer – “This only affects Joe’s property. This property must meet all of Harmony’s buffering requirements. At this time the Public Hearing was Closed. Mayor Turner presented a request to rezone from property owner. Jared asked, “Would this prevent him from building a single-family home if he changes is mind?” Matthew answered, “No.” Jared made a motion to approve the zoning map amendment, and therefore make a finding that the approval is consistent with the future land use Residential-Agricultural designation and that said approval is reasonable and in the public interest and furthers the goals of the Future Land Use Plan because public utilities are now available, and the RO zoning district preserves the residential character of the area. We have homemade ice cream and 67 Pizza scheduled to be here. Clay Lunsford will provide the music. Chris will get of other musicians that we might get. We are renting a stage to use for this Farmer’s Market. Chris made a motion to look into purchasing a stage (size we need and shipping cost) Brandon seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. The June Farmer’s Market will be on Flag Day. We will combine the two. We are looking for someone to sing the National Anthem. WEB SITE: Grant is making progress on the website. He will have more information for us next month. Mayor had talked with Kadre Campbell about managing our social media. He asked the Council if they would like to meet him? Answer was “Yes, and we can negotiate a price at that time.” Also, we should give him a short trial period. CEMETERY FENCE: We have received quotes from Daniel Harris and Tim Souther to power wash the fence and columns at the cemetery, the outside of the community building and the shelter and area at the park. Harris’ quote was $1,700.00 and Southers’ quote $1,800.00 However Harris was disqualified because he did not have liability insurance. Jared made a motion to hire Tim Souther. Chris seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. BATHROOM REMODEL AT COMMUNITY CENTER: Cory Pennell has given us a quote of $4,800.00 to do the job. Price will be split 50/50 with the Community Center Board. Any action was tabled until after the July 4th breakfast. MURAL: Scotty showed picture of mural done by Studio73. Everyone liked them and said we needed to get some quotes. NEW BUSINESS: CAMERAS AT WWTP: A request was presented from plant operator for more cameras at the plant. We have a quote from Cass Computer Repair to install two more cameras at the plant for $2,694.32. Chris made a motion to accept the quote and have the cameras installed. Jared seconded. Motion carried 4-0. WEB-SITE: We will meet at 6 P.M. on June 12th to view progress on the web-site with Grant. 2024 – 2025 BUDGETS: Clerk asked for vote to accept the 2024-2025 General Fund budget – Scotty made a motion to approve and accept the 2024-2025 GF budget. Brandon seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. Jared made a motion to approve and accept the 2024-2025 Sewer Fund budget. Scotty seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. PROPERTY TAX RATE: Scotty made a motion to let the 2024-2025 Property Tax rate remain at $ .13 per $100.00 valuation. Chris seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. We will meet on June 26th at 6:00 p.m. to approve the 2023-2024 budget amendments. ENGINEERING FIRM: We need to find an engineering firm to get prince to extend our sewer lines to the Tomlin Rd. exit. We will use Love’s water for re-claimed water. Lowes would love to tap in with us. We need to annex our property at the WWTP into the city limits. This will be a satellite annexation. Love’s plans to open in January – February, 2026. North Iredell High School struggles with their sewer system. TRASH SERVICE: We hope to have quotes from Waste-Pro (Matt Myers), Home Team Waste (Mooresville) and Waste Pro by the July 8th meeting. We would consider buying our own cans (300). Scotty made a motion to close the meeting to go into closed session to discuss personnel matter. Mayor Turner called meeting back into session. Tractor show was great. Asked council to think about what price we should charge to rent out the field for other events. Mayor wants to establish an Events Committee to work on some events. Question was asked “Do you want to have two meetings a month to keep the meetings from being so long? Mayor has moved money from Money Market at First Horizon to a Money Market at First Bank. ADJOURNMENT: As there was no other business: Scotty made a motion to adjourn. Jared seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. ______________________________ ________________________ Town Clerk Mayor

title: Board of Aldermen Meeting - March 3, 2025
text: Town of Harmony 3389 Harmony Hwy, Harmony, NC 28634 704-546-2339_________ DATE: March 3, 2025 TIME: 6:00 PM ATTENDEES: Sean Turner, Mayor Chris Pierce, Council Member Scotty Harris, Council Member Brandon Angell, Council Member Wanda Edwards, Town Clerk / Finance Officer AGENDA: Call to Order: Mayor Turner Invocation: Jared Clark Pledge of Allegiance: Approval of minutes: Brandon Angell made a motion to approve the February 3rd, 2025 minutes. Jared seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. Brandon made a motion to approve the minutes of the closed session meeting. Jared seconded the motion carried 4-0. PUBLIC COMMENT PERIOD: Citizens should sign up with the Town Clerk to speak to the board by 3:00 pm on Thursday prior to the meeting on Monday night . Each speaker is asked to limit comments to 3 minutes. The total comment period will be 15 minutes or less. At the time of sign-up, speakers should state their subject or the matter of concern. Thank you for your consideration of the Town Council, staff, and other speakers. OLD BUSINESS: Spring In the Park: Time has been changed to 12 pm – 5 pm. Mayor Turner will have a Mayor’s team challenge Corn-hole tournament. COMMUNITY CENTER BATHROOMS: Cory is almost ready to go back to work. PLAYGROUND: We have not heard back from the company in Mooresville that was cc0ntacted about repairs to the step going up to the slide and the swing. EDDIE GAITHER: He has removed his personal belongings from the café building and returned the key. He has the power turned off to the building. We will change the water to Town of Harmony. Mayor knows of someone who is interested in building in that location. We need to have a called meeting to get a plan in place. We’re waiting to see what Napa is going to do. Mayor has spoken with Kith Howard about the possibility of selling his land. COMMUNITY CENTER COUNTER TOPS: Chris brought up that we need to get an estimate to replace the counter tops in the kitchen. Mayor said we would wait until after the July 4th breakfast to see how much money was raised. We need the electrical outlet that we use to plug in the Christmas Tree at the square and the Christmas lights on Hwy 901 W repaired. SEWER: Jeff spoke about quotes he has received for repair vs replace for pump on 21 south. The pump that is out of commission was put in when the sewer system was installed. Pump # 2 was rebuilt about 3 years ago. Clearwater came and pulled pump # 1 to see if it could be rebuilt. Jeff likes Clearwater because they will come out and pull the pump and then put it back in the hole. Quote from Clearwater for repair is $15,492.38 and for a new pump $26,559.40. We have a quote from Pete Duty for a new pump for $14,825. Plus cost of freight and tax and Jeff said we would also have to purchase a $5,000.00 adapter. With Clearwater we will not need the adapter. Jared is in favor of Clearwater and purchasing a new pump. After checking with financial director, Brandon said he was in favor of rebuilding the pump. Jared agreed. Jared made a motion to have Clearwater rebuild pump # 1 at 21 south pump station. Brandon seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. Pete Duty gave us a quote of $1,115.00 for a spare pump for the EQ basin at the WWTP. Mayor said that we will proceed with purchasing this pump. Jeff also has a quote from Pyle and Maryland Bio Chemicals that he needs to purchase by April. TOMLIN ROAD PROJECT: Mayor and Sean met with Benji Thomas and Ben Shelton on Wednesday to talk about sewer line going across Ben’s property. It would also go across 3 other properties. Not to go on right of way or easements. Benji is to get estimate of cost of putting in line. Jim Boser has a program that could possibly get us money to use for infrastructure. Ours is kind of project they want to help with. County Manager says they will let us borrow money and we can pay them back with the grant. USDA only guaranteed 45% of the money we need. Mayor is suggesting we do a preferred contractor and that it be Country Boy – he only wants our engineer in charge. Country Boy (Chris Cartner) says if the deal doesn’t work where the County loans us the money, he will loan us the money until the grant comes through. We need to have a higher connection rate for businesses. We may bring in an additional 30-35,000 gallons per day. We need to have a rate set for commercial businesses. We need to have a budget meeting in May. ADJOURNMENT As there was no other business, Scotty made a motion to adjourn. Chris seconded. title: Board of Aldermen Meeting - March 4, 2019
text: Town of Harmony Meeting Minutes Town of Harmony North Carolina 3389 Harmony Highway, Harmony, NC 28634 704-546-2339 DATE: March 4, 2019 TIME: 7:00 PM ATTENDEES: Lee Matney, Mayor John Ray Campbell – Alderman Julia Clanton – Alderman Doug Galliher – Alderman Scotty Harris - Alderman AGENDA: Call to Order: Mayor Matney Invocation: Alderman Harris Pledge of Allegiance: Alderman Clanton Approval of previous Months Minutes Julia Clanton made a motion to approve the minutes of the February 4th meeting – Scotty Harris seconded the motion. Motion carried. Public Comment Period: Notes on the Comment Period Each speaker is asked to limit comments to 3 minutes. The total comment period will be 15 minutes or less. Citizens should sign up with the Town Clerk to speak to the board by 3:00pm on the Thursday prior to the meeting on Monday night. At the time of sign-up, speakers should state their subject or the matter of concern. Speakers should be aware the Town Board is interested in hearing the concerns of the speakers; however speakers should not expect Board action or deliberation on the subject matter brought up during the Public Comment segment. Thank you for your consideration of the Town Council, staff, and other speakers. . Melissa Gaither from the Harmony Library spoke to the group regarding activities planned at the library. She told the group that the planetarium had been at the Baptist Church Life Center on Saturday, March 2nd and would be at the Fire Department on Friday, March 8th, and at the Harmony Elementary School gym on Wednesday, March 13th. Old Business: Town Clerk told the group that Brian Gantt will get a quote to us for proposed CPA work by the May meeting. New Business The Board was presented with a proposal for a tap into the sewer line for Richard Johnston on Little Wilkesboro Road. Question was asked “who usually does the tap?” Scotty said that Country Boy has done the taps in the past. Julia stated that they do a good job. Scotty suggested that we get no more bids. Julia said that we need to collect the tap cost before the work begins. The cost of the tap is to be paid by Mr. Johnston. Mr. Johnston said that he did not receive the letter regarding the impact fee at the time the sewer system was installed. John Ray said that letters were sent to owners of vacant lots. Julia said that we should not waive the impact fee as this sets a precedent for others who may have to pay the impact fee. All were in agreement. Mayor Matney asked the Council for approval to sign the Approval of Emergency Debris, based on a competitive solicitation that included price, contract with the county. This sets us to receive aid from FEMA. In the event of an emergency, the companies approved by the county come in to assist with clean up. Harmony is not under the umbrella of the county. Each municipality has to sign a contract. There is no cost unless we use the services. Julia Clanton made a motion for approval for Mayor Matney to sign the Approval of Emergency Debris contract. Scotty Harris seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. Mayor Matney brought up for discussion a proposal to work on an ordinance concerning cows inside the town limits of Harmony. We are having complaints on cows getting out and onto other person’s properties. Louis Rodriquez on the north end of Harmony Highway has fenced in his front yard and put in cows. We have sent him a copy of the ordinance prohibiting cows in the town limits and a copy of the general statue dealing with the fines that could be involved if ordinances are not followed. Mayor will contact Mr. Rodriquez to tell him that he has to remove the cows. Council asked Mayor begin work on such an ordinance and bring it back to the council. Julia asked that we have the pavers, that were around the Town Limits sign that was destroyed in a wreck, be removed and stored until the new sign is installed. Julia asked about cemetery clean up before Easter. First cleanup is scheduled for April 29th. Scotty recommended putting a notice on the sign to remind people of the cleanup. Lee will take care of this and he is also going to put a notice in the Statesville Record and Landmark. Scotty asked about the sign at Barker’s store blocking view of those pulling out onto Hwy 21. Mayor Matney has talked with DOT and they said the sign is back the appropriate amount. Joe Barker will not move the sign. Scotty asked about the probability of getting the speed limit on Hwy 21 in front of his house to Powell Bridge Road be changed from 45 mph to 35 mph. Adjournment John Ray Campbell made a motion to adjourn the meeting. Doug Galliher seconded the motion. Motion carried. Town Clerk___________________________________Mayor____________________________

title: Board of Aldermen Meeting - March 4, 2024
text: Town of Harmony 3389 Harmony Hwy, Harmony, NC 28634 704-546-2339 DATE: March 4, 2024 TIME: 4:00 PM ATTENDEES: Sean Turner, Mayor Chris Pierce - Council Member Scotty Harris - Council Member Jared Clark – Council Member Brandon Angell – Council Member Wanda Edwards – Town Clerk AGENDA: Call to Order: Mayor Turner Invocation: Council Member: Scotty Harris Pledge of Allegiance: Brandon Angell was absent from the meeting. Approval of minutes: Scotty Harris made a motion to approve the February 5th, 2024 minutes. Chris Pierce seconded the motion. Motion carried 3-0. Jared Clark made a motion to approve the February 13th, 2024 minutes. Scotty seconded the motion. Motion carried 3-0. Jared made a motion to approve the February 16th minutes. Scotty seconded the motion. Motion carried 3-0. Public Comment Period: Each speaker is asked to limit comments to 3 minutes. The total comment period will be 15 minutes or less. Citizens should sign up with the Town Clerk to speak to the board by 3:00 pm on the Thursday prior to the meeting on Monday night. At the time of sign-up speakers should state their subject or the matter of concern Speakers should be the Town Board is interested in hearing the concerns of the speakers, however speakers should not expect Board action or deliberation on the subject matter brought up during the Public Comment segment. Topics requiring further investigation will be referred to the appropriate town officials or staff and may be scheduled for a future agenda. Thank you for your consideration of the Town Council, staff and other speakers. Melissa Gaither from the Harmony Library spoke to the group about activities at the library. The NC Reads Book Club began today. They have activities planned for the children throughout the month. The summer reading program runs from June 3rd through July 27th. She said that in the past the town had made a $500.00 donation and asked if we would like to do so again. OLD BUSINESS: FARMERS MARKET: Mayor Turner has reached out to farmers to discuss the farmer’s market. He is proposing a monthly market to begin late April through August possibly from 4p.m. until 7 p.m. with music, etc. to go along with the farmer’s market. We could possibly use the lot next to the library. The Mayor said that we might be able to eventually get a Golden Leaf Grant. We need to appoint a manager (possibly Doug and Tim). They would be asked to go to the Farmers Market meeting and possibly set up a table to get more information about how the farmer’s market should be set up. Everything sold will need to be locally grown, not purchased and brought in to sell. Jared said he was in favor of doing the market once a month. Chris likes the idea of music and having it close to the library. The Mayor asked if they were o.k. with asking Doug to be manager. All agreed they were. THEATRE BLDG: Mayor Turner has a meeting with potential investors Tuesday or Wednesday about buying the property. He will report back to the Board next month. PLANNING BOARD: Mayor Turner has talked with Matthew Todd. Matthew pointed out that we have an ordinance stating that the Planning Board will be made up of the Mayor and Council Members. We need to amend this ordinance before we can appoint the five members of the Planning Board. The ordinance should read that the Planning Board will consist of five (5) members appointed by the Mayor and Town Council. We will put out announcements 10 days prior to our April 6th meeting that we will have a public hearing to amend this ordinance. A vote will then be taken at the meeting to amend the ordinance. WEB SITE: Mayor Turner gave Board members a copy of a proposal from Grant Gaither to update and improve our website. He asked them to take it home and read it. We may be able to reduce the price some. He said we need our own branding. He told board members to call Grant with any questions. Jared said he would have a conversation with Grant. Mayor Turner said that we will set up a meeting with Grant later this month. NEW BUSINESS: TELAMON: Sabryna Brown and Norma Lucas from Teleman spoke to the group about what Telamon has to offer. They work with farmers and farm workers. Workers have to be citizens or have permission to work and provide certification. They help those who have worked in agriculture, dairies, tobacco, cotton, canneries, poultry/food processing industry for two years and want to go to school , find a new job or gain new skills. They can also help with obtaining a high school diploma, or adult basic education. They help with career assessment and guidance, applying for college and financial aid, internships, resumes and interviewing skills and job placement. Mayor Turner will host a meeting with some of the local farmers and Sabryna and Norma to explain the program to them. Chris thinks it is a good to partner with them. CEMETERY FENCE: Need to get quotes to clean the cemetery fence and also to pressure wash the community building. TREES AT WWTP: We have two quotes to cut the trees at the WWTP, Loren Speaks dba MAKAVERY TREE in the amount of $1,800 and Country Boy Landscaping, Inc, in the amount of $9,500.00. Chris made a motion to accept the bid from MAKAVERY TREE. Jared second the motion. Motion carried 3-0. LINDA DR: Mayor Turner presented a bid from Country Boy Landscaping, Inc, to remove and replace the existing 18” CMP at the end of Linda Dr. in the amount of $9,225.00. Scotty made a motion to accept their bid and have them do the work. Chris seconded the motion. Motion carried 3-0. TELEMETRY: Waiting to hear from installer about an installation date. TRASH CANS: Mayor gave board a price list for trash cans in the event that Republic increases the cost of collecting our residential trash weekly and we need to go another route. CAPITAL PROJECT ORDINANCE: Mayor Turner read a Capital Project Ordinance for the Town of Harmony Asset Inventory and Assessment Project No. AIA -W-ARP-0110 (Attached) Scotty made a motion to adopt the ordinance. Jared seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. ADJOURNMENT: As there was no other business: Scotty made a motion to adjourn. Jared seconded the motion. Motion carried 3-0. ______________________________ ________________________ Town Clerk Mayor

title: Board of Aldermen Meeting - March 7, 2022
text: TOWN OF HARMONY MEETING MINUTES Town of Harmony 3389 Harmony Hwy, Harmony, NC 28634 704-546-2339 DATE: March 7, 2022 TIME: 4:00 PM ATTENDEES: Lee Matney, Mayor N Sankey Gaither - Council Member Julia Clanton - Council Member Doug Galliher – Council Member Scotty Harris – Council Member AGENDA: Call to Order: Mayor Matney Invocation: Council Member Harris Pledge of Allegiance: Council Member Clanton Approval of minutes: Scotty Harris made a motion to approve the February 7th minutes. title: Board of Aldermen Meeting - May 1, 2023
text: Town of Harmony 3389 Harmony Hwy, Harmony, NC 28634 704-546-2339 DATE: May 1, 2023 TIME: 4:00 PM ATTENDEES: Lee Matney, Mayor N Sankey Gaither - Council Member Julia Clanton - Council Member Doug Galliher – Council Member Scotty Harris – Council Member Wanda Edwards – Town Clerk AGENDA: Call to Order: Mayor Matney Invocation: Council Member Harris Pledge of Allegiance: Council Member Clanton Approval of minutes: Julia Clanton made a motion to approve the April 3rd minutes. Infrastructure Grant – Lee will be going to Raleigh to meet with Representatives on May 24th regarding the $250,000.00 grant. Julia said the back fence at the cemetery needs to be cleaned up. title: Board of Aldermen Meeting - May 6, 2019
text: Town of Harmony Meeting Minutes Town of Harmony North Carolina 3389 Harmony Highway, Harmony, NC 28634 704-546-2339 DATE: May 6, 2019 TIME: 7:00 PM ATTENDEES: Lee Matney, Mayor John Ray Campbell – Alderman Julia Clanton – Alderman Doug Galliher – Alderman Scotty Harris - Alderman AGENDA: Call to Order: Mayor Matney Invocation: Alderman Campbell Pledge of Allegiance: Alderman Clanton Approval of previous Months Minutes Julia Clanton made a motion to approve the minutes of the April 1st meeting – Scotty Harris seconded the motion. Motion carried. Public Comment Period: Notes on the Comment Period Each speaker is asked to limit comments to 3 minutes. The total comment period will be 15 minutes or less. At the time of sign-up, speakers should state their subject or the matter of concern. Thank you for your consideration of the Town Council, staff, and other speakers. . Council welcomed Jay and Maureen Lytsell and Glen Belcher to the meeting. Old Business: Discussion was held on lowering the speed limit inside the city limits of the town to 35 mph. Scotty Harris made a motion to have the speed limit set at 35 mph. Julia Clanton seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. Maureen and Jay Lytsall spoke to the group about the problems they are having with Jose Rodriquez who lives next door having cows and goats in his front yard and roosters in his back yard. Chicken wire is the only fencing for keeping the cows and goats in the pasture. It was suggested that they talk with the Sheriff’s Department. The Board will also continue to work to help solve the problem. Board was presented with an Engagement Letter from Gantt Malzi Associates, CPPAs to work with town office to ensure that we are compliant with government accounting procedures and that in transferring accounting systems, all numbers rolled up correctly. Board members were satisfied with their proposal. Julia Clanton made a motion to accept the Engagement Letter as written. Doug Galliher seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. Julia Clanton asked about having speed bumps installed on John Deere Dr. due to people speeding. Mayor said that all of the residents along the road would need to sign a petition requesting that speed bumps be installed. Town Clerk will write up a petition and Julia will get it signed. Mayor will check with Ruby Pierce to see if she is in agreement. Signage will have to be put up stating that speed bumps have been installed. Town Clerk told the Board that our contract with Ceres for emergency debris has been sent in and that Ceres has accepted the contract. A signed copy of the agreement is on file in the town office. New Business Tent for cemetery – John Ray said that the grave diggers from Statesville will no longer dig graves in the Harmony Cemetery. Drew Williard from Yadkinville, NC is willing to dig the graves for us. We will pay him for digging the grave and the funeral home will reimburse the town for this expense. John Ray brought up a discussion concerning the need for the town to buy a tent to be used for the family at the grave site. The funeral homes have a tent that can be used for the family at the grave site, but Drew would have to drive to the funeral home to get the tent. John Ray brought up a discussion of paying Drew to drive and get the tent verses the town purchasing a tent. The cost of a tent the size that is needed is approximately $2,360.00. If we purchase the side flap, that is an additional $460.00. Drew will dig the grave for $600.00. He will dig the grave and put up and take down the tent for $650.00. Julia thought that in order for the town to recoup the expense of purchasing the tent, the cost the funeral home charges the family for using the tent should come to the town. Julia asked Mayor Matney to call Bill Brater at Bunch Johnson to see if they would pay the town for using our tent. After discussion, the matter of purchasing a tent was tabled until the next meeting. Julia made a motion to hire Drew Williard to dig the graves for the town at a cost of $600.00 per grave site. John Ray seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0 Grose Street – Mayor spoke to the Council about repaving Grose Street. He has obtained 3 bids for the work – JEM’s Grading & Paving $45,350.40; T.L. Huffman - $65,855.00; and Country Boy Landscaping - $49,889.84. After discussion, the Council wants to look at the road before a decision is made. Council will also look at the road condition on Hayes Street. Adjournment Julia made a motion to adjourn. John Ray seconded. Motion carried. text: Town of Harmony 3389 Harmony Hwy, Harmony, NC 28634 704-546-2339 DATE: May 6, 2024 TIME: 4:00 PM ATTENDEES: Sean Turner, Mayor Chris Pierce - Council Member Scotty Harris - Council Member Jared Clark – Council Member Brandon Angell – Council Member Wanda Edwards – Town Clerk AGENDA: Call to Order: Mayor Turner Invocation: Council Member: Scotty Harris Pledge of Allegiance: Jared Clark was absent from the meeting.
