text: Town of Harmony 3389 Harmony Hwy, Harmony, NC 28634 704-546-2339_________ DATE: May 7, 2025 TIME: 6:00 PM ATTENDEES: Sean Turner, Mayor Chris Pierce, Council Member Scotty Harris, Council Member Brandon Angell, Council Member Wanda Edwards, Town Clerk / Finance Officer AGENDA: Call to Order: Mayor Turner Invocation: Scotty Harris Pledge of Allegiance: Chris Pierce was absent from the meeting. Brandon Angell made a motion to approve the minutes of the April 7th, 2025 meeting. Scotty Harris seconded the motion. Motion carried 3-0. Scotty made a motion to approve the minutes of the April 22nd, 2025 meeting. Brandon seconded the motion. Motion carried 3-0. PUBLIC COMMENT PERIOD: Citizens should sign up with the Town Clerk to speak to the board by 3:00 pm on Thursday prior to the meeting on Monday night . Each speaker is asked to limit comments to 3 minutes. The total comment period will be 15 minutes or less. At the time of sign-up, speakers should state their subject or the matter of concern. Speakers should be aware that the Town Board is interested in hearing the concerns of the speakers, however, speakers should not expect Board action or deliberation on the subject matter brought up during the Public Comment segment. Topics requiring further investigation will be referred to the appropriate town officials, or staff and may be scheduled for a future agenda. Thank you for your consideration of the Town Council, staff, and other speakers. Ms. Elizabeth Hannis spoke to the group about the fact that the sewer bill is based on water usage. She said that when she fills her swimming pool or waters her garden, that water does not go through the septic tank and it is not fair that her sewer bill is based on that water usage. She was reminded that her bill is adjusted one time when she fills the swimming pool. Mayor Turner told her that we have no way of regulating water usage to tell how much is used for the filling the pool or watering the garden. He suggested that she might want to get an irrigation meter. Water would be cheaper than going through the sewer. OLD BUSINESS: Spring In the Park: Event was very successful. Food vendors did very well. We had a good number of people attend. Farmers Market will begin the 2nd Friday in May. Skinners Food Truck has asked to come back and serve. Information on Farmers Market will be posted on our face book page. COMMUNITY CENTER BATHROOMS: Mayor has not talked with Cory Pennell to get scheduled. PLAYGROUND: We will work with Kan Contracts to get old swings dismantled in preparation for new swings. Street Light Cedarvale – Power lines are underground along Cedarvale. Duke Power will be coming in to replace some poles, Mayor will talk with them about what it will take to get street lights. NEW BUSINESS: Maintenance Log on Equipment – Wanda and Doug will get a list of equipment and prepare a log. Jeff’s contract has been updated to specify that he carry Workers Comp Insurance and that he hire another licensed person to serve as back-up operator. Back-up Operator can be a Grade 1. Jeff will work 10-20 hours per week. We will meet with Ms. Dixon on Thursday at 6 p.m. Clerk discussed the Iredell-Rowan Hazard Mitigation Plan Resolution and asked for a vote that we enter into the plan with Iredell County. Scotty made a motion to adopt the resolution. Brandon seconded the motion carried 3-0. Mayor Turner spoke about going to City Vision. He said it was good to mingle with other town leaders. He learned from other mayors of towns our size that they experience some of the same problems that we do. He learned that Harmony needs to do some strategic succession planning. He spoke with engineers who were interested in our plans for the cafe and would work with us to secure grants. He met several people he would like to bring before the council. Rural Water talked about a “collections” apprentice. He would work under Jeff as a way to eventually get his license. Mayor will get information to Council. Mayor will be meeting with Black Elected Officials in July. Sewer Line Extension: Pat Harrigan sent out the appropriations letter for 2025-2026. Mayor is working with Centralina Council of Government for a Community Block Grant Funding. May get up to $3,000,000. Mayor thinks it looks favorable. Lowe’s will hopefully contribute to the line being built. Sewer Rates: Normally municipalities charge double rate for outside city limit services or ask for annexation. We need a rate for businesses. Jared said that we need to raise rates at least a small amount for all customers. Mayor wants to offer those who are not connected, but are paying the flat rate a chance to connect to the sewer and we will waive the $1500.00 impact fee. Brandon made a motion to offer anyone who has been paying the flat rate a chance to connect to the sewer and we waive the impact fee. Scotty seconded the motion. Motion carried 3-0. An addendum was added to the motion that we stipulate that the waiving of the impact fee run for a time period of July 1, 2025 – July 1, 2026. Brandon suggested a better way to schedule “special meeting “ might be to use a Google Calendar. As there was no other business, Scotty made a motion to adjourn. Brandon seconded. Motion carried 3-0. _____________________________________ _________________________________ Wanda Edwards, Town Clerk Sean Turner, Mayor

title: Board of Aldermen Meeting - November 4, 2021
text: TOWN OF HARMONY MEETING MINUTES Town of Harmony 3389 Harmony Hwy, Harmony, NC 28634 704-546-2339 DATE: November 4, 2021 TIME: 4:00 PM ATTENDEES: Lee Matney, Mayor N Sankey Gaither - Council Member Julia Clanton - Council Member Doug Galliher – Council Member Scotty Harris – Council Member AGENDA: Call to Order: Mayor Matney Invocation: Council Member Harris Pledge of Allegiance: Council Member Clanton Approval of minutes: Scotty Harris made a motion to approve the October 4th minutes. Julia Clanton seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. Public Comment Period: Each speaker is asked to limit comments to 3 minutes. The total comment period will be 15 minutes or less. Citizens should sign up with the Town Clerk to speak to the board by 3:00 pm on the Thursday prior to the meeting on Monday night. At the time of sign-up speakers should state their subject or the matter of concern Speakers should be the Town Board is interested in hearing the concerns of the speakers, however speakers should not expect Board action or deliberation on the subject matter brought up during the Public Comment segment. Topics requiring further investigation will be referred to the appropriate town officials or staff and may be scheduled for a future agenda. Thank you for your consideration of the Town Council, staff and other speakers. Melissa Gaither from the Harmony Library told the group about programs planned for November. Tony Brewer, from Eddie Carrick, CPA, who performed the town audit , came to speak to the group about the 2020-2021 audit. He thanked the council for allowing them to do the audit. The Town of Harmony received a clean audit. He reminded the group that the audit is a public document and can be view by anyone who requests to do so. The Fund Balance is 558% up 154% from 404% in 2020. The General Fund has had a very good year. The revenue in the sewer fund is down. This is due in part by the school being closed due to COVID. Expenditures were up. Miscellaneous expenses were up due to $5,000.00 being spent to apply for a grant. We also spent $17,000.00 to repair a road going up to the sewer plant on W. Memorial Hwy. Revenue was less than expense by $69,000.00. Collection rate is 98.61% which is above state rate. Changes from Local Government Commission – They now send a letter to the town and ask how we plan to mitigate the deficiency. Auditor tells us what the problems are and we respond directly to the LGC on how we intend to fix them. This came about because LGC got complaints that Boards sometimes did not know of problems. We have 60 days from time Tony tells us of the problem (November 1st ) to respond to the letter. ALL board members are required to sign the letter. Ad Valorem Taxes – Tony says to keep an eye on the collections to be sure they do not fall below 3%. A significant deficiency that was noted in the audit was a lack of segregation of duties in the office. He noted that this is often the case in small towns where it is cost prohibitive to have more than one person in the office. Tony also noted a change that is coming to the audit process. As the process is now. Tony prepares the financial statements during the audit. In the future, if the town spends over $100,000.00 in federal or state funds, Eddie Carrick, CPA will not be able to prepare the financial statements. We will be required to have a “yellow book” audit. Joe Haney comes in to do the review before the audit. Tony has set up a separate company aside from Eddie Carrick, CPA so he can do the financial statements, and then under Eddie Carrick, CPA he will be able to do the audit. Mayor Matney asked if the $100,000.00 was for General Fund and Sewer Fund each? Tony said it was combined. The Board thanked Tony for coming and presenting this information to the council. Jeff Jones who is the recently hired ORC for the Waste Water Treatment Plant spoke to the council to bring them up to date about WWTP. He also introduced his nephew, Jason Jones who is working with him at the plant. Jeff told the group that Natalie Narron from Rural Water will be here on November 16th to do an efficiency study on ways that we may be able to save on electricity costs. OLD BUSINESS: Park Fence - Privacy fence – Ron Bell from Yadkinville has done a preliminary survey of the fence lines at the park. He says we are on Mr. Pierce’s property about 4’ in one place. Julia said we should put the new fence on our line. Sewer Rates – Will be discussed in depth at the December meeting. Clerk will get each council member a copy of the rate study this week so they can study it before the meeting. NEW BUSINESS: Christmas Parade – December 5th at 2 p.m. Complaint about overgrown field as you turn into Hayes St. – Buddy says it has been mowed Christmas Gift Cards from Sharpe’s Catering - Marty Liles, Jeff Jones, Jason Jones, Wanda Edwards, Tim Trivette and Glen Belcher. Christmas Bonus’ – Harmony VFD $1000.00; Tim Trivette $75.00; Dennis Tomlin $50.00; Christine Rosario $50.00; Wanda Edwards $300.00. text: Town of Harmony 3389 Harmony Hwy, Harmony, NC 28634 704-546-2339 DATE: November 4, 2024 TIME: 6:00 PM ATTENDEES: Sean Turner, Mayor Chris Pierce - Council Member Scotty Harris - Council Member Jared Clark – Council Member Brandon Angell – Council Member Wanda Edwards – Town Clerk AGENDA: Call to Order: Mayor Turner Invocation: Mayor Sean Turner Pledge of Allegiance: Jared Clark was absent from the meeting. Mayor wants the town designated as an “Opportunity Zone”. This means businesses would get a tax break to come in and build. Matthew Redmond and others are interested if we make Harmony an Opportunity Zone. Jeff told the group that he had to re-do the scope of work on the AIA grant so they could do videoing of the lines. We also had to re-do the original scope of work for the $250,000. grant because we have already done some of the work that was listed in that scope. Mayor has a teleconference Wednesday regarding the line to the Tomlin Mill exit. CONTRACTS: Discussion was held about renewing Jeff’s contract as ORC for the town. Jeff thinks we should leave it as a recurring contract until he or the board wants to make a change. Mayor wants to leave Jeff under same contract until we have a re-evaluation or a new contract. title: Board of Aldermen Meeting - October 1, 2019
text: TOWN OF HARMONY MEETING MINUTES Town of Harmony 3389 Harmony Hwy, Harmony, NC 28634 704-546-2339 DATE: October 7, 2019 TIME: 7:00 PM ATTENDEES: Lee Matney, Mayor John Ray Campbell - Council Member Julia Clanton - Council Member Doug Galliher – Council Member Scotty Harris – Council Member AGENDA: Call to Order: Mayor Matney Invocation: Council Member Campbell Pledge of Allegiance: Council Member Clanton Approval of previous month’s minutes: Julia Clanton made a motion to approve the 8/29/2019 minutes. Doug Galliher seconded the motion. Motion carried. Julia made a motion to approve the 9/9/2019 minutes. Scotty Harris seconded the motion. Motion carried. Public Comment Period: Each speaker is asked to limit comments to 3 minutes. The total comment period will be 15 minutes or less. Citizens should sign up with the Town Clerk to speak to the board by 3:00 pm on the Thursday prior to the meeting on Monday night. At the time of sign-up speakers should state their subject or the matter of concern Speakers should be the Town Board is interested in hearing the concerns of the speakers, however speakers should not expect Board action or deliberation on the subject matter brought up during the Public Comment segment. Topics requiring further investigation will be referred to the appropriate town officials or staff and may be scheduled for a future agenda. Thank you for your consideration of the Town Council, staff and other speakers. Chris Cartner, who has recently purchased the old Reavis Funeral Home and the former Methodist Church, spoke to the group about his frustration of how to get our ordinances enforced (specifically as related to the property owned by Chad Gilreath beside and behind his property). The Mayor told Chris that the town had hired a new attorney to help get our ordinances legal in order so these issues can be enforced. The County is of no help to us in so far as enforcing our ordinances and the property owner and renter do not care. Julia told Chris that the Town is with him and the property next to his is our first priority. Lee has been working on getting the ordinances corrected for 2 years. We have to have ordinances that are legally correct in order for them to be enforced. Julia assured Chris that the Board is taking his concerns seriously. When ordinances are corrected and enforceable, we are going to take immediate action. Melissa Gaither from the Iredell County Library thanked the Board for the $500.00 donation and told the group that with the money she hired a storyteller (Mrs. Barlowe) to come on October 30th for storytelling and a puppet show. She said next year the summer reading kick-off will be held at the Harmony Library. OLD BUSINESS: Mayor told the group that all of the concerns brought up by R.D. Gatton at the September meeting have been resolved with the exception of the “Welcome to Harmony” sign. The thought is that this sign be left where it is and a new “City Limit” sign will be put up at the city limit. Mural: John Stewart has been out to look at the location and will get us a price. Erosion Control: Matthew Todd had spoken to the Board about going with the County on erosion control. Lee has spoken with Mr. Lowry and Jimmy Reavis and they told him they could not separate what is county and what is state on their new properties. Julia and Scotty are not in favor of going with the county. Julia made a motion not to go with the county erosion control. Doug seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. Information Sign - Jonathan Elam gave the council a bid of $2,753.08 to refurbish the sign we have now. Council thinks this is too high. Doug Galliher said that he and Tim Trivette would work on cleaning up the sign. Cost should fall under dollar threshold of what Lee can spend without board approval. Harmony Night Out – October 8th – good attendance is expected. Town will have a table. Mayor asked council to be there. Roof – Dry-Tech Commercial Roofing will be here around 1st of November to install the new roof. Ms. Vogel said that we cannot foreclose on this property. She gave us her remedy: we clean up the property and send Mr. Lavoi a bill. If he does not pay the bill, then we can foreclose on the property. We have a quote from Tommy Thompson for the clean up in the amount of $1,850.00 but he wants to wait for weather to cool off. Doug asked if we can legally go on the property. Julia suggested that we hold off until our ordinances are corrected and then we let the property owner know what we are going to do. Julia suggested postponing a vote for the time being. Yearly Contracts: Tommy Thompson, Blake Renegar and Charles Trivette are not asking for an Increase in the amount of their contract if the Council decides to renew their contract in 2020. Tommy will add $90.00 to add the sewer line on Isa’s Lum. Julia asked if Charles will be reliable. Lee will talk with him. title: Closed Session - August 12, 2020
text: TOWN OF HARMONY PERSONNEL MEETING Town of Harmony 3389 Harmony Hwy, Harmony, NC 28634 (704) 546-2339 Mayor Lee Matney, Council Member Doug Galliher and Town Clerk Wanda Edwards met with Waste Water Treatment Plant employees Anthony Gilbert, J. D. Powell and Scotty Harris on August 12, 2020 at 3:00 p.m. Scotty opened the meeting with the invocation. Mayor Matney told the group that the council had been discussing (with the exception of Scotty) the direction we want to take in regards to the WWTP. Discussions have taken place about some of the problems at the plant and how to remedy them. We are in the process of applying for a Infrastructure Grant and finding a new ORC. Mayor Matney asked about their staying on at the WWTP and what changes they would like to see. Scotty – wants more cross training – when things are getting worn out, they need to be repaired or replaced. He would like to learn additional things at the plant Anthony – wants additional cross training so when someone goes on vacation, their job will be covered. J D said they could make time to do more cross training. At present they are working with only one pump. They are supposed to have a back-up. The check valve needs to be repaired. It is clogging the line. The bar screen at the plant on S. Hwy 21 has a broken winch that has never been repaired. (The bar screen catches everything). J D will get Barry Ehert to look about repairing the winch. State Inspector is coming on 8/18/2020. J D will talk with Ernie at Associated Metals about making the guards that need to be installed at the plant. UV lights on Bank 1 are not working. LED side 1 are not working at all. Mayor Matney asked Scotty, Anthony, and J D is they wanted to work for the town or work under a contract. All agreed that they wanted to be town employees. Anthony will be the ORC – Scotty will be the back-up ORC J D said that during normal routine they should expect to turn in 120 hours per month. If something goes wrong the number of hours will be higher. Anthony will do the samples. Danny Smith from Rural Water will come in and teach Anthony to do the DMR reports. Discussed what happens with blowers during a power outage – when power goes out, generator comes on and blowers work – when power is restored, and you turn the generator off, you have to manually turn the blowers back on. When power goes off, Anthony will go over and restart blowers. Town Clerk will contact Yadkin Valley Telephone about getting a phone and the internet installed at the WWTP. J D will talk with someone about getting SCADA on Scotty and Anthony’s phones. ______________________________ ______________________________ Town Clerk Mayor

title: Closed Session - July 20, 2020
text: TOWN OF HARMONY Town of Harmony 3389 Harmony Hwy, Harmony, NC 28634 (704) 546-2339 PERSONNEL MEETING The Town Board met in a called session on July 20th at 3 p.m. for the purpose of discussing the dismissal of Steven Lambert as Sewer Plant Operator. Present for the meeting were Mayor Lee Matney; Council Members – Julia Clanton, Buddy Gaither and Doug Galliher and Town Clerk Wanda Edwards. The meeting was opened with the invocation. Comments were: Buddy has spoken with Michael Campbell about the possibility of working at the sewer plant. He is not available. J D will stay if Steve is gone and he is pretty sure Anthony will stay. Joe Steele will not say or do anything as long as Steve is there. Pretty sure if he does come to work for the town, he will do a contract. Lee has spoken with Danny Smith from Rural Water. He can’t do any of the work for us, but he can come by every couple of weeks to check on things and let us know if we need to do something. Lee spoke with Kathy Payne at Cleveland – she told him it was hard to find a plant operator to work without a contract. Julia suggested that if someone presented us with a contract, we should not sign it until Ms. Dixon looks at it. Julia questioned if we should go ahead and fire him before we advertised for a replacement. Julia suggested that we go ahead and fire Steve and see if Joe will work on a monthly basis for a while. Comments: Steve says we are out of OSHA compliance No clear communication with town Not satisfied with his job performance Lee has told him to get an electrician and plumber to install what is needed at sewer plan to bring us into compliance with OSHA – has not been done. Lift station – Hwy 21 South – top has been up for at least 6 months J D is upset about raise – He does most of the running to the other plants – Anthony was hired to alleviate some of J D’s hours – that has not happened – he is doing Steve’s job Lee thinks we should get into OSHA compliance before firing Steve – J D said he will instill guards that are needed at the waste water treatment plant. Julia made a motion to un-table the discussion about Steve Lambert’s job performance at the sewer plant. Doug seconded the motion. Motion carried 3-0. Buddy made a motion to relieve Steve Lambert of his duties as ORC at the wastewater plant. Julia Clanton seconded the motion. Motion carried 3-0. Board will meet with Steve on August 3rd, 2020 at 6:30 p.m. Items of discussion: Job Performance OSHA violations not fixed in requested / reasonable time frame Failure to cross train all employees as requested Lack of communication As there was no other business to discuss, Julia Clanton made a motion to adjourn. Doug Galliher seconded the motion. Motion carried 3-0. ______________________________ ______________________________ Town Clerk Mayor

text: TOWN OF HARMONY Town of Harmony 3389 Harmony Hwy, Harmony, NC 28634 (704) 546-2339 PERSONNEL MEEETING The Town Council met on September 14th, 2020 at 4:30 p.m. to discuss the continue the continued employment of Steve Lambert. Scotty asked why this is just now being brought up. Doug said that it would be to our advantage for ORC and back-up to have Collection License. Question was asked “Will the town pay for Anthony’s continuing education & license renewal each year?” “ For 2 people?” Clerk read a letter to the board from Town Attorney Kathy Dixon concerning changes that she would like to see made to Steve’s proposed contract and her opinion of Steve as ORC. Julia said that when contracts are to be signed, she wants the board to adopt an ordinance that states that any contract approved must be signed by the Mayor, board members, and witnessed by the town clerk. title: Closed Session - September 24, 2020
text: TOWN OF HARMONY Town of Harmony 3389 Harmony Hwy, Harmony, NC 28634 (704) 546-2339 PERSONNEL MEETING The Town Council met on September 24th at 4:00 p.m. to discuss the issue of employment of Steven Lambert at the Waste Water Treatment Plant. Buddy Gaither made a motion to rescind a motion made by himself on July 20th, 2020 to fire Steve as ORC at the WWTP. Scotty Harris seconded the motion. Voting “yea” - Buddy Gaither, Scotty Harris, and Doug Galliher. Voting “nay” – Julia Clanton . Motion carried 3-1. Matter to be discussed before the Board – To accept the contract with Steve Lambert and have him continue as the ORC at the WWTP. Scotty – Is he going to be more accountable to the board – He will continue with his monthly reporting Julia – wants more than the Mayor’s signature on the contract – we are working on an ordinance to state that the Mayor and council members will sign contracts and town clerk will witness the signatures. We can’t adopt this ordinance until we open the town meetings up to the public again. Scotty – can he go back to work at the WWTP? Lee suggested that he go talk to Steve. Doug – wants to see Steve gradually begin to turn some of the responsibilities over to Anthony in the upcoming months and Steve step back some. Lee assured him that Steve will be training Anthony. Buddy asked if we can make a suggestion to Steve to hire Scotty back? Scotty would like for Lee to sit down with him and Steve to talk. title: Special Meeting - December 14, 2023
text: TOWN OF HARMONY MEETING MINUTES Town of Harmony 3389 Harmony Hwy, Harmony, NC 28634 (704) 546-2339 DECEMBER 14, 2023 6:00 pm PURPOSE OF THE MEETING: TO DISCUSS THE 2045 HORIZON PLAN PRESENT FOR THE MEETING: MAYOR TURNER, COUNCIL MEMBERS, BRANDON ANGELL, CHRIS PIERCE, SCOTTY HARRIS AND JARED CLARK, TOWN CLERK WANDA EDWARDS, ORC, JEFF JONES, MATTHEW TOOD FROM IREDELL COUNTY ZONING AND JIM DOBSON AND JEFF CHEEK. Matthew told the group that the plan was to have been adopted last week but was not due to opposition. This gave us the opportunity to discuss, add in things, make changes and decide what we want to do. The plan will be adopted next Tuesday, December 19th. Matthew said that Harmony had develop zoning with the county in 2006 when we had a planning board. Land Use Plan requires us to have a Planning Board in place. Harmony did not have a plan to show growth. The Horizon Plan puts an area around Harmony for us to decide what we want to do. The County will help with the growth plans. Jared asked what is next step when it is adopted? Somebody has to come by and ask for re-zoning. Sewer is main piece to figure out. Jared asked “are most small towns drawing a circle around area?” Matthew answered he has not heard of other small towns doing this. Mayor Turner told Mr. Joseph Blankenship in the audience that there is no multiple family home ordinance in the town. Discussion followed about taking the sewer lines 5 miles to Union Grove. Mayor Turner said the farmers between here and there are going to say “no.” He said the exit areas around Tomlin Rd. and Union Grove would be possible expansions. He stated that we need growth, but in the right way. Matthew talked to the group about an annex agreement with Statesville at Tomlin Mill Road. They will want to begin offering sewer there. We should consider a good offense. Statesville will be wanting roof tops. Mayor Turner said an Agriculture processing company wants to come to our area. Jeff Cheek said there was little interest in the plan 18 months ago. People like it the way it is. He said we are a prime location for an agricultural community. People would be more amicable to this type of land us Horizon 2045 plan. Jim Dobson – Horizon Plan is only a guide. It has been amended immensely. Town of Harmony has opportunity – economy has influence on what can or cannot be done. In order to take sewer to Union Grove, we will have to purchase right of way from farmers and it will be expensive. People who have elected you, expect you to be sensible and make good decisions. Matthew Todd is a fine gentleman and is there to help. Work with Commissioners and keep a good relationship with them. Life depends on water, air, food and national security. What quality of life would you like to see for you children and grandchildren? Jeff Cheek – What is reluctance for why more have not hooked up to sewer? Mayor Turner stated that there is nothing in our ordinances that prohibits multi-family homes. Jim Dobson – Don’t lose sight of the fact that most of our roads are farm to market roads. It is the policy of the State of North Carolina that traffic has to be so much for improvement. Jim Dobson – Farm Preservation – you don’t sign a binding contract. It is understood that you will keep it for a number of years. Do you want to restrict a landowner on what he can do with his land? Use your conscience. Jared – Are we proposing changing to plan tonight? Answer “No” Matthew - We need to look at plan and see if we want to make changes to our plan. This is just a guide for our Planning Board. Jared – Jeff, do you see a path to get us out of the hole we are in now? Jeff – We are trying to cut all expenses. Even if we cut more expense, we would still come up short. Being distressed allows us access to more grants. Mr. Blankenship has expressed an in building multi-family units for senior citizens inside the city limits. Mayor – I will be speaking at the Commissioners meeting to give an update for the Town of Harmony. ar Tuesday Night, December 19, 20223 , The Iredell County Board of Commissioners will vote to approve the 2045 Horizon Plan. As there was no other business, Jared made a motion to adjourn the meeting. Scotty seconded the meeting. Motion carried 4-0. ________________________________ ___________________________________ Town Clerk Mayor

title: Special Meeting - February 13, 2023
text: TOWN OF HARMONY MEETING MINUTES Town of Harmony 3389 Harmony Hwy, Harmony, NC 28634 (704) 546-2339 February 13, 2023 Present for the meeting: Mayor Lee Matney, Council Members – Julia Clanton, Doug Galliher, Scotty Harris, and Buddy Gaither and Town Clerk Wanda Edwards, and ORC Jeff Jones Purpose of the meeting: To reconsider going forward with the AIA grant On February 1, 2023 we received an e-mail from Matthew Rushing, AIA/MRF Program Manager asking for clarification as to whether or not we are declining funding for the AIA Grant. He explained that the AIA project funding is in no way tied to the Viable Utility program or Distressed designation. At this time, Harmony is not currently designated as distressed. He also said that being distressed cannot be superseded by local action. Once designated, units must meet the requirements laid out in NCGS 159G-45(b) before SWIA and the LGC can consider taking action to de-designate a distressed unit. We need to reconsider if want to go forward with taking the grant. We have already spent $5,000.00 to apply for the grant. We don’t have to pay the 10% match. Mayor, board clerk and ORC would be accountable to keep the plan on track. W.T. Sorrell from Withers and Ravenal was on the phone with us during the meeting. He told us that we would need to send out RFQs (Request For Qualifications) to several engineering firms. We will need to put advertisement in newspapers and on our website. We will need to send RFQ to more than 3 firms. He said engineer can help find funding for projects. We need to name all types of services we might want put into the RFQ. Mr. Sorrell said that we could e-mail the RFQ’s to engineers. Julia made a motion to proceed with the AIA grant. Buddy seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. ____________________________ ______________________________ Town Clerk Mayor

title: Special Meeting - February 27, 2020
text: TOWN OF HARMONY MEETING MINUTES Town of Harmony 3389 Harmony Hwy, Harmony, NC 28634 704-546-2339 The Town Council met on February 27th, 2020 at 4 PM with Steve Lambert. Sankey Gaither Town Clerk: Wanda Edwards The purpose to the meeting was to discuss operations at the Waste Water Treatment Plants. Comments from Steve Lambert were as follows: Maintenance and condition of plant: Screw Screen / Filter are operating Flow meter has been replaced and is operating Blower has been repaired and fastened to mount Disinfecting UV system is working properly Plant electrician is Ehret Electric Dorsett has been told not to come out unless called Return activated sludge pump – uses large compress to clean when it becomes stopped up. title: Special Meeting - January 25, 2024
text: TOWN OF HARMONY MEETING MINUTES Town of Harmony 3389 Harmony Hwy, Harmony, NC 28634 (704) 546-2339 January 25, 2024 9:00 a.m. PURPOSE OF THE MEETING: KICK OFF FOR THE AIA GRANT Present for the meeting: Mayor Turner, Council Member Brandon Angell, Town Clerk Wanda Edwards, Town ORC Jeff Jones, Rural Water Troy Cassidy, Iredell County Commissioner Melissa Neader and Jared Wright from McGill Associates. Jared told the group that McGill had offices in three states specializing in water and wastewater. We will be working with Jared out of the Hickory office. The Asset Inventory Assessment will be used to dive deeper into what is underground – do a condition assessment based on the metric system – identify projects that are priority – utilize the GIS maps – the AIA is a starting point of what needs to be done. Troy asked if they would go back and do an assessment plan – Jared answered “yes at the end of the span and they would also do a rate study.” Mayor Turner discussed about those connected to our sewer system but were not within the city limits of Harmony. Jared will be our project manager – he will give regular updates and expects to finish up the entire project in December, 2024. He will document every system component and will identify materials. We will have fields in the report for condition assessment. Jeff stated that we are beginning to see age on our system. He also said that the AIA gives a road map for future planning. Mayor Turner acknowledged that we a distressed system, but he also noted the progress we have made from the figures in the 2022 audit and the 2023 audit. We will also need a Capital Improvement Plan to identify projects and plan for them. Jared stated that they were sensitive to rate increases. We have to let people know that we have a sewer system. Troy said that we have raised rates for the last two years. Discussed sewer system capacity – Troy spoke about those in the town who are not connected to the sewer and how it will affect the capacity when the need arises for them to connect. He suggested that maybe we should have septic tank inspections. Melissa said that private companies are now allowed to do septic tank inspections. Sean said that some of our lift stations have a small flow while others have a lot, Sean said that before we start extending our sewer lines, we need to be providing sewer on all of our streets. We will put out communications to sewer customers as needed when McGill begins working out in the fields. Sean thanked everyone for coming and concluded the meeting. _____________________________ ______________________________ Town Clerk Mayor

title: Special Meeting - January 28, 2025
text: TOWN OF HARMONY MEETING MINUTES Town of Harmony 3389 Harmony Hwy, Harmony, NC 28634 (704) 546-2339 January 28, 2025 Purpose of the meeting: To decide on purchase of new Christmas Decorations for poles Present for the meeting: Mayor Turner, Council Members, Brandon Angell, Jared Clark, Scotty Harris and Chris Pierce and Town Clerk Wanda Edwards. Mayor explained to the group that some of our decorations were not in good shape and we need to get some new ones. Town Clerk has been working with Jay Mallas from Mosca Design to come up with some pricing for new decorations. Clerk presented Council with 3 proposals (1) $30,916.92 to replace all of the decorations (2) $19,613.93 for 26 new decorations plus a 4’ extension to the height of our Christmas tree and (3) $16,705.11 for 26 new decorations. After discussion, Scotty made a motion that we purchase the 26 new decorations for $16,705.11. Brandon seconded the motion carried 4-0. Jeff’s Contract – Mayor told the group that Jeff did not accept the proposal he had presented to him. Discussion was held regarding Jeff’s lack of Worker’s Comp Insurance – Jeff said he did not have to carry Worker’s Comp if he is under 3 employees. He was asked to spend 4 hours per day at the plant 5 days per week. Jeff said his charge to the town is figured in at 2-3 hours per day and that he does not charge us when he is called back. Regarding reporting odors to DEQ – he says they do not want that reported to them. Reports – Mayor still wants reports- he wants to know when he is here and what he is doing. We do not want DEQ here all the time. Jeff still uses soda ash. Mayor asked him to do ring and cap repair at Highland Pt. manhole – he was going to check for taps that may be connected to sewer without our knowledge. We are paying the most of all the places he works. We are in the middle of AIA – not a good time to make change. Mayor told Jeff he is not trying to push him away. If we double our capacity, we are going to have a lot more work to do. Lines will have to be flushed every quarter. Mayor wants a weekly report. Jared asked if we terminate him, does it affect AIA? text: TOWN OF HARMONY MEETING MINUTES Town of Harmony 3389 Harmony Hwy, Harmony, NC 28634 (704) 546-2339 March 12, 2025 6:00 PM Purpose of the meeting: Meet with Town Attorney – Kathy Dixon Present for the meeting: Mayor Sean Turner; Council members, Chris Pierce, Scotty Harris, Jared Clark and Brandon Angell (by phone) and Town Clerk Wanda Edwards. Ms. Dixon spoke about the group being stewards of the town money. She told about the Sunshine Law and said everything we do must be open and accessible. She cautioned that we could only talk town business in the meeting hall. No town business is to be discussed outside of that room. She said that jobs must be bid out. Every bid is to come back sealed and opened in the meeting hall. We let anyone wanting to bid on a project know the parameters of the bids. If someone wins a bid and fails to uphold the bid, we can fire them. We would not have to accept a second bid from them. Question was asked, that if, for example, Tommy who does our mowing, does not increase his price, do we have to re-bid his contract. Ms. Dixon said it is best to re-bid the contract. She said Tommy’s contract needs to be re-written to show the number of people he has working for him when he mows the town areas and the amount of time it takes to complete. Ms. Dixon wants to see all contracts before they are signed or agreed upon. She also told the group that anyone can come in and ask to see someone’s contract and we are obligated to show it to them. Mayor Turner asked her about Jeff needing to carry Workers Comp. insurance. She told him that Jeff only has to have Workers Comp. if he has three or more employees. We could carry him under the town’s workers Comp. Right of Way or easements regarding sewer line going to Love’s – Ms. Dixon said there was three ways of doing this: (1) annex property within three miles of the city (2) condemnation action (3) General Assembly says “do it” – they seize the property. We could do eminent domain to give notice of a lawsuit. Everybody has to be paid. NCDOT comes in and appraises the land. Question is “who is going to maintain the property?” It is major work to put in a sewer pipe. Mayor said there were four land owners. We will be putting in a 6” line. Ms. Dixon suggested that we do not get involved in NCDOT right of way. If we bring lawsuit against land owners, they have one year to answer the lawsuit and another year before it will go to court. We have to take the money that the NCDOT appraises the land for and the county will hold it until the lawsuit is settled. Ms. Dixson said the contractor had to be approved by Raleigh. Mayor said the county is willing to lend us the money while we are waiting for Helena money. USDA has a lot of strings attached. In the near future we need to set a meeting with Mayor, Ms. Dixon, the engineer with all the players. As there was no other business to discuss, Chris made a motion to adjourn. title: Special Meeting - March 13, 2023
text: TOWN OF HARMONY MEETING MINUTES Town of Harmony 3389 Harmony Hwy, Harmony, NC 28634 (704) 546-2339 March 13, 2023 6 P.M. SEWER MEETING Mayor Matney welcomed everyone to the meeting. Invocation was given by Scotty Harris. Julia Clanton led the group in the Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag. Mayor Matney told the attendees that the purpose of the meeting was to discuss the financial status of the sewer system. Present for the meeting was Mayor Lee Matney, Council Members – Julia Clanton, Scotty Harris, Doug Galliher, Buddy Gaither, Town Clerk – Wanda Edwards – Town CPA – Joe Haney and from Rural Water – Troy Cassity. Troy told the group what Rural Water does for the town. He has worked with the town for two years. He told the group that the Town had received a letter from the NC State Treasurer/LGC warning that we were in danger of becoming a distressed system (namely that we do not take in enough revenue to offset the expense). Last year we had to raise sewer rates to show LGC that we are working towards solving the problem. If the state deems us distressed, they can take over the sewer system and then we would have no say in the rates. Troy did a study of the rates, of the number of people paying. We have 241 customers. Number connected to sewer to sewer – 180. Number not connected – 61. Those not connect, now pay $34.50 per month. Those connected pay $37.00 per month. Troy proposed to raise all to $40.00 per month. He encouraged any not connected to sewer to go ahead and connect. Joe explained that the Sewer Fund has to operate independent of the General Fund. He explained that the Town has reached the LGC radar and has to explain how we are trying to rectify the situation. Cost to maintain the system has gone up and rates were not raised. Question was brought up when the rate increase would go in effect. Julia answered they would go in effect in July, 2023. We will consider whether business rates will be higher than residential. Question was brought up about expanding lines. Before expanding lines, we must do a feasibility study – we want to be responsible before we undertake anything else. Scotty told the group that we have made a lot of improvements to the WWTP. Buddy said we are trying to do better, a lot of problems were inherited. Doug said we have learned a lot and we are working hard. Several in the group asked questions about connecting to the system. title: Special Meeting - March 17, 2025
text: TOWN OF HARMONY MEETING MINUTES Town of Harmony 3389 Harmony Hwy, Harmony, NC 28634 (704) 546-2339 March 17, 2025 6:00 PM Purpose of the meeting: To discuss Jeff Jones contract Present for the meeting: Mayor Turner; Council members - Scotty Harris, Jared Clark, Brandon Angell and Chris Pierce; Town Clerk, Wanda Edwards and ORC, Jeff Jones Mayor Turner called the meeting to order. Each council member was given a copy of Jeff’s contract that was to be discussed. Jeff told the council that he does not have to carry Workers Comp insurance with less than three employees. He said his son is a licensed operator and is his back-up for the plant. He is also talking with someone else to see if they would be interested in serving as a back-up operator. Jeff told the group that he cannot do 4 hours a day, 5 days a week at the plant. Our permit sets no specific amount of time he has to be there. He has to be there 5 days per week to record the temperature. Jeff said it is mandatory to be on site 5 days per week. When Jeff first applied for job, he asked for $4,500.00 per month, but agreed to do the job for $4,000.00. He worked 2 years and 2 months before the board gave him a raise. Bill rate for call out was originally $20.00 per hour, now it is $70.00. He noted he has never charged the town for any call out. Jared said everything in contract needs to be titled in Jeff’s LLC name. Jared wants him to have workers comp insurance. Jeff is agreeable, but might have to charge the town for it. Jeff said “overage hours” would be anything after 5 pm. Mayor does not agree. Discussed hours worked total for month. Jeff will do progress reports weekly. Council wants report on Thursday. Jared asked how many hours per day on contract? Brandon asked how many per week? Mayor asked “at Sparta, all you take care of is the plant, what if you did that here? What if we hired a collections operator and paid them $16.00 per hr? Jared likes weekly hourly requirement and documentation of running of plant. After discussion, it was decided that Jeff would work between 10-20 hours per week. Jared wants contract to be on a one year review. Agreed Upon: List of tasks with accountability to list / no time sheet / try different templets for weekly reporting for 4 weeks / focus on not getting sued – getting things done. Mayor wants update on back-up operator. Chris wants update follow ups on motors, etc. and better contact between Jeff and Mayor. Scotty thanked Jeff for the hard work he has put in at the plant. He told the group what a mess Jeff walked into and how he has turned the plant around. He said Jeff is doing a great job and he appreciates all he is doing. As there was no other business, Brandon made a motion to adjourn. Chris seconded the motion. carried 4-0. ____________________________ ______________________________ Town Clerk Mayor

title: Special Meeting - October 23, 2023
text: TOWN OF HARMONY MEETING MINUTES Town of Harmony 3389 Harmony Hwy, Harmony, NC 28634 (704) 546-2339 CALLED MEETING OCTOBER 23, 2023 4 P.M. PURPOSE OF THE MEETING: TO DISCUSS SEWER IMPACT FEE Present for the meeting: Mayor Lee Matney, Council members Scotty Harris, Doug Galliher, Buddy Gaither, Town Clerk Wanda Edwards, ORC Jeff Jones, and Town Attorney Kathy Dixon. Also present for the meeting Sean Turner, Brandon Angel, Matt and Sherry Wilson. Mr. Angel of 105 Tomlinson Ave. is in the process of connecting to the town sewer system. Mr. & Mrs. Wilson of 3426 Harmony Hwy are also anticipating connecting to the system. They are protesting the $1,500.00 impact fee that must be paid when someone connects to the sewer system due to an earlier conversation Mr. Angel had with Doug Galliher in the town office. In conversation, Doug said that if you connected to the sewer before the end of the year, the impact fee would be waived. This statement was incorrect and pertained to a statement made by Troy Cassidy at a meeting in March, 2023 when he was discussing ways we might persuade the people inside the city limits who were not connected to the sewer to connect to consider connecting. Ms. Dixon told Mr. Angel and the Wilson’s that anything said in the town office was not legal and binding. It was only legal if it was said in the Town Conference Hall. Also, this was never a decision made by the board, voted on and recorded in the minutes. She told the group that the town borrowed federal money to build the sewer system and with that loan there was an ordinance that stated that anyone connecting to the sewer after the initial start up period would be required to pay the $1,500.00 impact fee and this ordinance was recorded as a part of the loan and could not be broken. Mr. Angel also had stated that to connect to the system he would have to bore under the road. He asked Jeff if there was a problem with the pipe under the road who would be responsible for repairing the pipe. Does the town repair it? Jeff replied that the town is only permitted for mains, lift stations, and sewer plant. He also said that ever since he has been working for the town everyone who connects to the sewer has paid the $1,500.00 impact fee. At this point, Scotty made a motion to adjourn the meeting. Doug seconded the motion. Motion carried. ______________________________ ______________________________ Town Clerk Mayor

title: Special Meeting - September 12, 2024
text: TOWN OF HARMONY MEETING MINUTES Town of Harmony 3389 Harmony Hwy, Harmony, NC 28634 (704) 546-2339 September 12, 2024 Purpose of the Meeting: Discuss purchase of Harmony Café property from Eddie Gaither Present: Mayor Turner, Council Members: Scotty Harris, Chris Pierce, Jared Clark, Brandon Angell and Clerk Wanda Edwards. Guest: Luke Martin, Real Estate Attorney Mayor Turner has talked with former Mayor Matney who told him to be careful of this property and watch for buried gas tanks at the location of the old Gregory’s Grocery and in front of the Napa Store. Mayor thinks we need to have this investigated. Asking price for the property is $250,000.00 – 25,000.00 down with contract. Carolina Soil Investigations does investigations for gas in the ground. They are environmental specialist. Phase #1 – not too invasive – Phase # 2 more intense. Their charge for sample $2,500.00 - $3,000.00. No one is sure about asbestos in the building. Demo quote from Terry Miller – if we assume and tear down Napa ($15,000.00) if we tear down café, theatre and Napa at the same time he will do it for $45,000.00. Set back is 40 ft. from the white line (structure) no matter what. Parking cannot be like it was before. Mayor has talked with DOT – if we ever need to do a traffic circle, there is enough room as it is now. Tomlin Road would be a problem. Best bet would be to take Tomlin Rd south. Storm drain comes to corner of Gaither’s property. Mayor wants DOT to re-do entire storm drain system. DOT is claiming ownership of storm drains. Jared said he thought main reason for buying property was to fix roads. Mayor said we need to talk with Ted Bud about Rural Vitalization Project. They will help with funding. Mayor has a meeting Wednesday with a large business that wants to come to Harmony (baseball park). We want to position ourselves to be in charges. Want to attract motels, restaurants, etc. at Tomlin Rd., We need to plan ahead. This is how to save our farm land. Jared said the first piece is fixing the traffic problem. Storm drains and power lines have to be redone before anything can be done. Mayor said ball has to get rolling someway. We are getting some money from Golden Leaf. Mayor said before we move too fast, Eddie is offering to sell the garage property and the café property for $750,000.00 with him vacating 1/01/2025 or selling it for $725,000.00 and him vacating on 1/01/2026. Mayor said this is not a good number. He suggested when we make an offer on the café, we make it contingent with first refusal on second property. Luke said with contract $25,000.00 is earnest money. We should focus on café side with refundable earnest money, 45 days due diligence (60 preferable) and 90 days close. If environmental problem shows up when survey is done, Eddie must disclose to future purchasers. If we tear down wall next to Napa, they will have to re-route their water lines. We need to find the septic tanks and grease trap. Don’t make an offer until the study is done. NC has a trust fund to help pay for cleanup. Luke told the group, “do not be afraid of higher prices – we can always negotiate down.” Put first Right of Refusal in our contract. Jared made a motion to offer $200,000.00 for the property. $25,000.00 earnest money – 45 days closing with a 15 day extension period – First Right to Refusal to garage property. Brandon seconded the motion. Motion carried. Luke will send the offer letter to Eddie. Brandon made a motion to adjourn. Jared seconded. Motion carried 4-0. _________________________ ______________________________ Town Clerk Mayor

title: Special Meeting - September 19, 2022

title: Special Meeting - September 23, 2024
text: TOWN OF HARMONY MEETING MINUTES Town of Harmony 3389 Harmony Hwy, Harmony, NC 28634 (704) 546-2339 September 23, 2024 Purpose of the Meeting - Harmony Café Property Present for the meeting: Mayor Turner, Council members: Scotty Harris, Chris Pierce, Jared Clark, Brandon Angell and Clerk Wanda Edwards Mayor opened the meeting with prayer Mayor Turner has received a response from Eddie Gaither and his wife refusing our offer of $200,000.00 for the Harmony Café property. They are standing firm on their $250,000.00 asking price. Mayor explained to Eddie the cost of testing the soil and demolition to explain our offer. Mayor told group that we could hold off on demolition. USDA has a demo grant. USDA could look at town hall and see if we need a new town hall and assist with that. Rural Development can assist a business owner with a low cost loan. Board wants to see business on the property. Suggested that Town could loan money for business. Amount of space that is there is good. Water going into Napa goes in from the old theatre. Napa’s septic is under the café building. Napa does not have a sewer tap. They will have to spend money or sell. Discussed Eddie’s garage property that he also wants to sell. Garage property is smaller than café property .67 acres with a 40’ set back. Question was asked, “Do we want to move forward on the cafe property?” All agreed that we should give him the asking price of $250,000.00. Jared said that we should also purchase the garage. Others disagreed on the garage property. Mayor Turner said the value of what he is asking is not there. Financially it is not a good idea. Jared said if we own the property, we can change the intersection. Mayor told him that he had talked with DOT and they said we would have enough room for a traffic circle as things are now. Scotty reminded that Hwy 21 is a federal highway and Hwy 901 is a state highway so we could not make changes without their approval. Mayor suggested that we put in the contract that Eddie gives us 10 business days to decide if we want to buy the garage and he has to prove that he has another valid offer of someone wishing to purchase the property, Mayor said that if someone wanted to open a restaurant or business on the café property, a USDA loan might be available. He thinks Mr. Blankenship can get a USDA loan for affordable housing for his project. Jared made a motion to put in full asking price of $250,000.00 for the Harmony Café property with a 10 day first right of refusal for the garage property. Brandon Angell seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. Chris Pierce made a motion to adjourn. Jared seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. ______________________________ ______________________________ Town Clerk Mayor

title: Special Meeting - September 3, 2021
text: TOWN OF HARMONY MEETING MINUTES Town of Harmony 3389 Harmony Hwy, Harmony, NC 28634 (704) 546-2339 September 3, 2021 Meeting with Jeff Jones, Troy Cassidy, Mayor Matney, Doug Galliher and Buddy Gaither and Clerk Wanda Edwards present. Notes taken: We are permitted at 80,000 gal per day / with 7 lift stations – Jeff wants to look at the lift stations. Wanted to know if we used Dorset. He is very familiar with Missions telemetry – very easy to repair – he can repair it himself – Dorset is very expensive – live units should only be at WWTP – not necessary at lift stations. Jeff has a lot of background experience. He is currently the Utility Director for the Town of Boonville and manages the water for Rhonda. He is interested in expanding. He will submit testing to Statesville Analytical. He or his assistant will personally take the samples to Statesville. Jeff will be working 120 hours per month. Charge each month will be the same whether it is a 4-week month or a 5-week month. 10% of lines will be cleaned annually. He has his own insurance. Town will not be reimbursing him for the cost. He will do one after hours call per month at no cost to the town. After that the cost will be $20.00 per hour. The Town will not be asked to buy any tools – he will provide his own. We will 1099 him for tax purposes. He will create a work order flow system with invoice each month and he will send a more detailed maintenance log report of work performed. His son will be working with him and will be here 5 days per week. He will check in at the office each day. Jeff will work with county inspector to be sure we are notified when a sewer tap is installed. He knows local vendors that may be able to save us some money. Jeff has someone who will be his back-up. He will not need J D or Anthony. ORC will be here 4 days a week to do sampling – back-up 1 day per week. We will be able to get in touch with Jeff 24 hours a day – 7 days a week. He is asking $4,500 per month. After Visiting WWTP he noted: Plant has great potential Noted pump on its side – worst thing you can do for a pump 3 grates were removed Hoses – trip hazard Affluent had a lot of floatable solids Both clarifiers had pop-ups Council will meet with Jeff on September 9th at 4 p.m. – Jeff’s phone number is 336-466-0887. ______________________________ ______________________________ Town Clerk Mayor

title: Special Meeting - September 9, 2021
text: TOWN OF HARMONY MEETING MINUTES Town of Harmony 3389 Harmony Hwy, Harmony, NC 28634 (704) 546-2339 September 9, 2021 The Harmony Town Council met with Jeff Jones. Present for the meeting was Mayor Matney, Council members Julia Clanton, Scotty Harris, Doug Galliher, Buddy Gaither and Town Clerk Wanda Edwards. Notes: He has been in wastewater since December of 1999. He is Public Works Director in Boonville. He has a Grade 4 Certification in Collections and a Grade 2 in Waste Treatment Plant. A Contract was discussed - He would like a 30 day notice before either party terminates. He can do a one year contract and then go month to month if that is what the board wants. Jeff’s son and nephew will be helping him. He will cover them under his liability and worker’s comp. insurance. He noted that we use the Dorsett Scada System which costs about $5,000.00 for a unit. If it goes out, only Dorsett can fix it and they will charge tech time and cost of parts. Jeff likes the Mission unit which costs $3,600.00 for a unit and he is able to repair it himself. It was decided that if he were hired, before major repair or purchase, he would call Mayor Matney or Scotty Harris for approval. Scotty made a motion to hire Jeff Jones as ORC of our WWTP with a one-year contract. Julia seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. Julia Clanton made a motion to fire Steve Lambert from his position as ORC of our WWTP. Scotty seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. As soon as his contract is up, he is terminated and we will not renew the contract. He is to be notified on September 10th, 2021 that his termination is effective October 10th, 2021. Julia made a motion that we make a counter offer to Jeff Jones and offer him $4,000.00 salary as ORC. If he doesn’t accept or makes another, we go with original price. Buddy Gaither seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. Julia made a motion to adjourn. Scotty seconded the motion. Motion carried 4-0. ______________________________ ______________________________ Town Clerk Mayor

Whenever in this code or in any ordinances of the Town, any act is prohibited or made or declared to be unlawful, where no specific penalty is provided therefore, the violation of the provision of the code shall be punished by a fine, not to exceed one hundred ($100.00) dollars for each separate violation. Each day any violation of the code or of any ordinance shall continue shall constitute a separate offense. 1 CHAPTER 1 – THE CODE ARTICLE 1 – USE OF THE CODE SECTION 1.1 – Definition and Rules of Construction In the construction of this Code and of all ordinances, the following definitions and rules of construction shall be observed unless inconsistent with the manifest intent of the Board or the context clearly requires otherwise. BOARD: The words “the board: shall mean the Board of Aldermen of the Town of Harmony. COMPUTATION OF TIME: The time within which an act is to be done shall be computed by excluding the first and including the last day; and if the last day is Saturday, Sunday or a legal holiday, that day shall be excluded. COUNTY: The word “county shall mean the County of Iredell in the State of North Carolina, except as otherwise provided. MAYOR; The words “the Mayor” shall mean the Mayor of the Town of Harmony. MONTH: The word “month” shall mean a calendar month. NUMBER: Words used in the singular include the plural and words used in the plural include the singular number. OATH: The word “oath” shall be construed to include an affirmation in all cases in which, by law, an affirmation may be substituted for an oath, and in such cases the words “swear” and “sworn” shall be equivalent to the words “affirm” and “affirmed.” OWNER: The word “owner,” applied to a building or land shall include any part owner, joint owner, tenant in common, joint tenant or tenant by the entirety, of the whole or a part of such building or land. PERSON: The word “person” shall include a corporation, firm, partnership, association, organization and any other group acting as a unit as well as an individual. PERSONAL PROPERTY: The words “personal property” includes every species of property except real property as herein defined. PRECEDING, FOLLOWING: The words “preceding” and “following” shall mean next before and next after respectively. PROPERTY: The word “property“ shall include real and personal property. REAL PROPERTY The words “real property” shall include land, tenements, and hereditaments. SIDEWALKS The word “sidewalk” shall mean any portion of a street between the curb line and the adjacent property line intended for the use of pedestrians. SIGNATURE The words “signature” or “subscription” include a mark when the person cannot write. STATE The word “state” shall be construed to mean the State of North Carolina, except as otherwise provided. STREET The word “street” shall mean and include any public way, road, highway, street, avenue, boulevard, parkway, alley, lane, or bridge and the approaches thereto within the Town. TENANT The words “tenant” or “occupant” applied to a building or land shall include any person who occupies the whole or a part of such building or land whether alone or with others. TIME Words used in the past or present tense include the future as well as the past and present. TOWN The words “the town” shall mean the Town of Harmony in Iredell County, North Carolina, except as otherwise provided. WRITING The words “writing” and “written” shall include printing and any other made to represent words and letters. YEAR The word “year” shall mean a calendar year. SECTION 1.2 – Section Designations The headings of the several sections of this Code are intended as mere catchwords to indicate the contents of the section and shall not be deemed or taken to be titles of such sections nor as any part of the section, nor, unless expressly so provided, shall they be so deemed when any of such sections, including the catch lines, are amended or reenacted. 9/2/26, 2:20 PM ordinances file:///var/folders/19/pqx_nm4x6sn68f1wx6trwdgr0000gn/T/paperclip-run-lac-1523-f6306006-244-YpDu7e/ordinances.html 12/48 SECTION 1.3 – Damaging Ordinances Prohibited No person shall tear or deface any of the Town ordinances. SECTION 7.25 – Ordinance prohibiting the unlawful use of engine and compression brakes (“Jake Brake Ordinance”) APPROVED AND ADOPTED BY THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF HARMONY, NORTH CAROLINA THIS THE 3RD DAY OF DECEMBER 2018. a. Purpose: The purpose of this ordinance is to prohibit the excessive, loud and unusual or explosive use of engine and compressed air-braking devices within designated areas in the Town of Harmony. b. Definitions: For the purposes of this ordinance the following words and phrases are defined as follows: (1) “Engine retarding brake” means a “Dynamic Brake”, “Jake Brake”, “Jacobs Brake”, “C-Brake”, “Paccar Brake”, transmission brake or any other engine retarding brake system that alters the normal compression of the engine and subsequently releases that compression. c. Prohibitions: It shall be unlawful for the driver of any vehicle to use or operate or cause to be used or operated within the incorporated areas of the Town of Harmony, State of North Carolina any engine brake, compression brake or mechanical exhaust device designated to aid in the braking or deceleration of any vehicle that results, in excessive, loud or unusual, or explosive noise from such vehicle, unless such use is necessary to avoid imminent danger. Such prohibitions shall be applicable only to those public highways or portions specifically identified in this Chapter. d. Areas of Prohibition: The prohibition set forth herein shall apply to the following highways in the Town of Harmony or portions thereof: 1. Highway 21 / Harmony Highway 2. Hwy 901 / Memorial Highway e. Signage: Signs stating “VEHICLE NOISE LAWS ENFORCED” OR “ENGINE BRAKE ORDINANCE ENFORCED” may be installed at locations deemed appropriate by the Town Board to advise motorists of the prohibitions contained in this ordinance, except that no sign stating “VEHICLE NOISE LAWS ENFORCED” or “ENGINE BRAKE ORDINANCE ENFORCED” shall be installed on a state highway without a permit from the North Carolina Department of Transportation. The provisions of this ordinance shall be in full force and effect even if no signs are installed. f. Exceptions: Emergency vehicles shall be exempt from the applications of this ordinance. g. Enforcement: This ordinance is deemed to be a town infraction. It shall be enforced pursuant to Chapter 7 of the Town of Harmony Code of Ordinances. h. Adoption: This ordinance will take effect upon final publication.
